text: भारतेंदु हरिश्चंद्र का जन्म 9-सितंबर, 1850 को वाराणसी के एक संपन्न, प्रतिष्ठित तथा साहित्यानुरागी परिवार में हुआ था। उन्होंने 1867 में कवि-वचन सुधा नामक साहित्यिक पत्रिका का प्रकाशन आरंभ किया। उन्होंने 1873 में हरिश्चंद्र मैगज़ीन नामक साहित्यिक पत्रिका का प्रकाशन आरंभ किया। उनके पिता गिरधर दास स्वयं एक प्रतिभाशाली कवि थे, जिनसे उनकी आरंभिक साहित्यिक अभिरुचियाँ अत्यंत गहराई से प्रभावित हुईं। वर्ष 1865 में जगन्नाथ मंदिर की यात्रा के दौरान वे बंगाल नवजागरण के बौद्धिक तथा सांस्कृतिक प्रभावों से परिचित हुए। इसी अनुभव ने उनकी रचनात्मक चेतना को सामाजिक सुधारों की ओर उन्मुख किया। तत्कालीन सांस्कृतिक-साहित्यिक गतिविधियों, विद्वत्परंपरा तथा सामाजिक जागरूकता ने उनके व्यक्तित्व-निर्माण में निर्णायक भूमिका निभाई। उनके नेतृत्व में विकसित साहित्यिक कालखंड को भारतेंदु युग अथवा नवजागरण काल कहा जाता है, जिसकी अवधि सामान्यतः 1869-1900 मानी जाती है। अल्पायु में ही माता-पिता की मृत्यु और तत्कालीन बौद्धिक गतिविधियों के निरंतर संपर्क ने उनके दृष्टिकोण को पूर्णतः बदल दिया, और केवल चौंतीस वर्ष की अल्पायु में 6 जनवरी 1885 को उनका निधन हो गया। भारतेंदु ने हिंदी पत्रकारिता को जनचेतना, सांस्कृतिक पुनरुत्थान तथा सार्वजनिक विमर्श का सर्वाधिक सशक्त माध्यम बनाया। उन्होंने कविवचन सुधा, हरिश्चंद्र मैगज़ीन और बालबोधिनी जैसी लोकप्रिय पत्रिकाओं का सफलतापूर्वक संपादन किया। इन प्रकाशनों ने हिंदी पत्रकारिता को नई दिशा प्रदान की और समाज के विविध ज्वलंत प्रश्नों पर खुली चर्चा के लिए उपयुक्त तथा विश्वसनीय मंच उपलब्ध कराया, जबकि इससे पहले अनेक हिंदी पत्र पाठकों तथा संसाधनों के अभाव में बंद हो चुके थे। उनके निबंधों, यात्रा वृत्तांतों और संपादकीय लेखन ने हिंदी गद्य के क्षेत्र को अत्यंत व्यापक तथा समृद्ध बना दिया। उन्होंने साहित्य तथा सार्वजनिक जीवन में हिंदी के अधिकाधिक प्रयोग की निरंतर वकालत की, जिससे उत्तर भारत में खड़ी बोली हिंदी आधुनिक साहित्यिक अभिव्यक्ति के सर्वाधिक सुदृढ़ माध्यम के रूप में सर्वत्र प्रतिष्ठित हुई। निज भाषा उनकी सुप्रसिद्ध तथा प्रेरणादायक रचनाओं में गिनी जाती है। आधुनिक हिंदी रंगमंच की आधारशिला रखने वाले रचनाकारों में भारतेंदु का स्थान सर्वोपरि तथा अविस्मरणीय माना जाता है। उनके प्रमुख नाटकों में अंधेर नगरी, भारत दुर्दशा, सत्य हरिश्चंद्र और नीलदेवी सम्मिलित हैं। इन नाटकों में व्यंग्य, सामाजिक आलोचना तथा नैतिक विषयों का अद्भुत समन्वय दिखाई देता है। वर्ष 1881 में रचित अंधेर नगरी नाटक में उन्होंने मनमानी सत्ता और कुशासन पर तीखा व्यंग्य प्रस्तुत किया। वर्ष 1875 में रचित भारत दुर्दशा नाटक में उन्होंने औपनिवेशिक शोषण और आर्थिक संकट पर गहरी चिंता प्रस्तुत की। इसी कारण यह रचना औपनिवेशिक शासन की आलोचना का प्रभावशाली उदाहरण मानी जाती है। राजनीतिक पराधीनता, आर्थिक कठिनाइयों और देश को पुनः खड़ा करने की आवश्यकता पर उनका बल इन रचनाओं में स्पष्ट दिखाई देता है। अनुवाद तथा साहित्यिक नवाचार के क्षेत्र में भी उनका योगदान उल्लेखनीय रहा। उन्होंने बंगला, संस्कृत, प्राकृत और अंग्रेजी की अनेक रचनाओं का अनुवाद और रूपांतरण किया। वर्ष 1868 में उन्होंने बंगला नाटक विद्यासुंदर का हिंदी में अनुवाद किया। उन्होंने संस्कृत नाटक मुद्राराक्षस का हिंदी में अनुवाद भी किया। शेक्सपियर के नाटक द मर्चेंट ऑफ वेनिस को उन्होंने दुर्लभ बंधु के रूप में रूपांतरित किया। उनकी कविताओं में भक्ति, देशभक्ति, सामाजिक परिस्थितियों और मानवीय पीड़ा का मार्मिक चित्रण मिलता है। प्रेम मालिका, प्रेम तरंग, मधुमुकुल और वर्षा विनोद उनकी उल्लेखनीय काव्य-कृतियाँ हैं। वैष्णव भक्ति से प्रेरणा लेते हुए उन्होंने सामाजिक समस्याओं तथा पारंपरिक रूढ़िवादिता को चुनौती दी। उन्होंने स्वदेशी को बढ़ावा दिया और प्रकाशनों के माध्यम से जनमत को प्रभावित किया। रसा उपनाम से लिखते हुए उन्होंने गरीबी, औपनिवेशिक शोषण और सामाजिक असमानता जैसे ज्वलंत प्रश्न उठाए। वर्ष 1880 में काशी में आयोजित एक सार्वजनिक सभा में विद्वानों ने उनकी साहित्यिक सेवाओं के सम्मान में उन्हें भारतेंदु की उपाधि प्रदान की, जिसका अर्थ भारत का चंद्रमा है। इसीलिए उन्हें आधुनिक हिंदी साहित्य, पत्रकारिता तथा रंगमंच के विकास में अग्रणी व्यक्तित्व के रूप में स्मरण किया जाता है।
title: Test #10: Bhartendu - Adhunik Hindi Sahitya Ke Janak

text: कुफरी जामुनिया भारत में बायोफोर्टिफाइड आलू की किस्मों के विकास में एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रगति का प्रतिनिधित्व करती है। एंटीऑक्सीडेंट, विटामिन और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों की प्रचुरता इसे आहार विविधता में सुधार और छिपी हुई भूख से निपटने के प्रयासों में एक मूल्यवान योगदान बनाती है। बायोफोर्टिफिकेशन पादप प्रजनन के माध्यम से फसलों की पोषक तत्व सामग्री में सुधार करता है, जिससे खाद्य पदार्थ प्राकृतिक रूप से आवश्यक पोषक तत्वों के उच्च स्तर प्रदान करने में सक्षम होते हैं। कुफरी जामुनिया के पल्प में 42.05 मिलीग्राम और छिलके में 80.66 मिलीग्राम एंथोसायनिन होता है। इसके पल्प में लगभग 42.75 मिलीग्राम विटामिन-सी भी मौजूद है। इसके पल्प में कैरोटीनॉयड की मात्रा लगभग 161 माइक्रोग्राम है। इसके अलावा, इस किस्म के पल्प में लगभग 22.77 पीपीएम जिंक और 32.23 पीपीएम आयरन पाया जाता है। पारंपरिक खाद्य सुदृढ़ीकरण के विपरीत- जिसमें प्रसंस्करण के दौरान पोषक तत्व जोड़े जाते हैं- बायोफोर्टिफिकेशन पोषण को सीधे फसल में समाहित करता है। यह आमतौर पर खाए जाने वाले खाद्य पदार्थों में पोषण की गुणवत्ता में सुधार करने का एक स्थायी और किफायती तरीका है। पर्याप्त कैलोरी सेवन के बावजूद छिपी भूख एक प्रमुख सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य चुनौती बनी हुई है। यह स्थिति तब उत्पन्न होती है जब लोग पर्याप्त मात्रा में भोजन तो करते हैं, लेकिन उनके आहार में आवश्यक विटामिन और खनिजों की कमी होती है। इस चुनौती से निपटने के लिए वैज्ञानिक बेहतर पोषण मूल्य वाली जैव-संवर्धित फसलों को तेजी से विकसित कर रहे हैं। अपने आकर्षक रूप, पाक बहुमुखी प्रतिभा और उत्तर भारतीय मैदानी क्षेत्रों के कई राज्यों के प्रति अनुकूलन क्षमता के साथ, कुफरी जामुनिया भविष्य में व्यापक स्तर पर खेती और उपभोग के लिए अपार संभावनाएं रखती है। प्रत्येक पौधा 10-12 मध्यम से बड़े आकार के कंद पैदा करता है। कुफरी जामुनिया मध्यम अवधि में पकने वाली आलू की किस्म है, जिसके पौधे मध्यम ऊंचाई वाले और चंदवा अर्ध-सघन होते हैं। इसके कंद बाहर से गहरे बैंगनी छिलके और अंदर से बैंगनी गूदे वाले होते हैं। ये उथली आंखों और भुरभुरी संरचना के साथ आयताकार होते हैं। बेहतर पोषण गुणवत्ता के साथ अच्छे कृषि प्रदर्शन को जोड़कर यह किस्म किसानों और उपभोक्ताओं दोनों को लाभ पहुंचाती है। साथ ही, यह दीर्घकालिक पोषण सुरक्षा को भी सुदृढ़ करता है। बायोफोर्टिफिकेशन अनुसंधान का एक महत्वपूर्ण परिणाम संवर्धित पोषण मूल्य वाली रंगीन आलू की किस्मों का विकास रहा है। इनमें लाल, बैंगनी और नीले गूदे वाले आलू शामिल हैं। इन आलुओं में एंथोसायनिन और कैरोटीनॉयड जैसे प्राकृतिक पिगमेंट होते हैं, जो इन्हें इनका विशिष्ट रंग प्रदान करते हैं। रंगीन आलू एंटीऑक्सीडेंट तथा आयरन और जिंक जैसे सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर होते हैं। अपने पोषण संबंधी लाभों के अलावा, कुफरी जामुनिया विभिन्न प्रकार के पाक उपयोगों के लिए उपयुक्त है। यह किस्म अपने आकर्षक बैंगनी रंग, भुरभुरी संरचना और सुखद स्वाद के लिए सराही जाती है। यह इसे पारंपरिक व्यंजनों और प्रसंस्कृत खाद्य उत्पादों दोनों के लिए उपयुक्त बनाता है। इसका विशिष्ट रंग व्यंजनों और प्रसंस्कृत खाद्य पदार्थों के दृश्य आकर्षण को भी बढ़ाता है। इसके अलावा, इन कंदों को निर्जलित उत्पादों  जैसे एंथोसायनिन युक्त दलिया, सूजी और आटे में प्रसंस्कृत किया जा सकता है, जिनका उपयोग विभिन्न खाद्य सामग्रियों में घटक के रूप में किया जा सकता है। बड़े पैमाने पर अपनाए जाने के लिए किसी फसल की किस्म का विभिन्न कृषि-जलवायु परिस्थितियों में विश्वसनीय प्रदर्शन करना आवश्यक होता है। कुफरी जामुनिया ने विभिन्न स्थानों पर किए गए परीक्षणों में स्थिर प्रदर्शन का प्रदर्शन किया है और इसे उत्तर भारतीय मैदानी क्षेत्रों में खेती के लिए अनुशंसित किया गया है। यह किस्म उन कई राज्यों के लिए उपयुक्त मानी जाती है जहां व्यापक रूप से आलू उगाया जाता है।
title: Test #11: Poshak Tatvon Se Bharpur Baigni Aaloo

text: 1857 की घटना से बहुत पहले, उसी प्रकार की एक घटना सन् 1817 में खुर्दा नामक स्थान पर घटित हुई थी। इस पर विचार करना शिक्षाप्रद होगा कि कैसे अंग्रेजों की औपनिवेशिक नीतियों के खिलाफ़ 19वीं सदी की शुरुआत से ही देश के विभिन्न हिस्सों में असंतोष निर्मित होने लगा था। खुर्दा, जो कि ओडिशा के दक्षिण-पूर्वी भाग में स्थित एक राज्य था, वह 19वीं शताब्दी की शुरुआत में 105-गढ़ों, जिनमें 60-बड़े और 1109-छोटे गांव सम्मिलित थे, एक जनबहुल उपजाऊ क्षेत्र था। इसके शासक, राजा बीरकिशोर देव को स्वःअधिकृत चार परगनाओं को तथा जगन्नाथ मंदिर के संचालन अधिकार समेत 14-गढ़जातों के प्रशासनिक उत्तरदायित्व को पूर्व में दबाव में आकर मराठाओं को सौंप देना पड़ा था। उनके पुत्र तथा उत्तराधिकारी, मुकुंद देव-द्वितीय इस दुर्दशा से विचलित थे। खुर्दा को अपने अधीन करने के तुरंत बाद अंग्रेज़ों ने राजस्व निवृत-ज़मीन पर कर लगाने की नीति अपनाई। इसमें राज्य के पूर्व सैनिक वर्ग, जिन्हें पाइक के नाम से जाना जाता था, उनका जीवन बुरी तरह से प्रभावित हुआ। इस नीति की भयावहता राजस्व की माँग में अनुचित वृद्धि और इस संग्रह के दमनकारी तरीकों से और बढ़ गई थी। इस कार्यवाही के फलस्वरूप 1805 और 1817 के बीच में खुर्दा से बड़े पैमाने पर लोग ज़मीन छोड़कर चले गए। फिर भी अंग्रेज़ों ने अस्थायी बंदोबस्त के तहत राजस्व भुगतान की नीति को चालू रखा जिसमें जमीन की उपजाऊ क्षमता तथा रैयतों की भुगतान की क्षमता की अनदेखी करते हुए हर वर्ष राजस्व की माँगों में वृद्धि की गई। यहाँ तक कि प्राकृतिक आपदाओं के समय में भी कोई उदारता नहीं दिखाई गई जबकि ओडिशा में ऐसी आपदाएँ अकसर आती रहती थीं। बकायादारों की ज़मीन को षड्यंत्रकारी राजस्व अधिकारियों या फिर बंगाल के सट्टेबाज़ों को बेच दिया गया। खुर्दा के विस्थापित राजा का वंशानुगत सेनानायक, जगबंधु विद्याधर महापात्र भ्रमरवर राय, जिन्हें लोग बक्सी जगबंधु के नाम से जानते थे, वह ऐसे बेदखल हुए जमींदारों में से एक थे। व्यावहारिक रूप से वे एक भिखारी बन गए थे। अपने तथा अपने जैसे ज़मीन से बेदखल हुए लोगों की ओर से संघर्ष करने का निश्चय करने से पूर्व प्रायः दो साल तक उन्होंने खुर्दा के लोगों के स्वैछिक दान से अपना गुज़ारा किया। बीते हुए वर्ष के साथ-साथ जो तकलीफ़ इन शिकायतों के साथ जुड़ गई थीं, वे थीं अंग्रेज़ों द्वारा इस क्षेत्र में चाँदी के सिक्कों का प्रचलन, इस नई मुद्रा में राजस्व के भुगतान पर जोर देना, खाद्य-सामग्री की कीमतों में अभूतपूर्व वृद्धि तथा नमक की आपूर्ति में कमी जो कि कंपनी के एकाधिकार नीति के चलते लगभग दुर्लभ हो गया था और जिसके कारण ओडिशा के पारंपरिक रूप से नमक बनाने वाले इस काम से वंचित हो गए थे, और स्थानीय ज़मींदारियों की कलकत्ता में नीलामी जिसके कारण ओडिशा में बंगाल के अनुपस्थित ज़मींदारों का आगमन हुआ। इसके अतिरिक्त असंवेदनशील तथा भ्रष्ट पुलिस प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था ने भी स्थिति को और दुष्कर बना दिया जिसके चलते होने वाले सशस्त्र संग्राम ने और भयावह आकार धारण कर लिया। 29 मार्च, 1817 को इस संग्राम की शुरुआत तब हो गई जब पाइकों ने बानपुर में स्थित पुलिस चौकी और अन्य सरकारी संस्थानों पर हमला कर दिया और सौ से अधिक लोगों की हत्या करने के साथ-साथ सरकारी खजाने में से एक बड़ी रकम लेकर चले गए। शीघ्र ही खुर्दा को केंद्र करते हुए इस घटना की लहर अलग-अलग दिशाओं में फैल गई। उत्साह से भरपूर ज़मींदार और रैयत, पाइकों के साथ मिल गए। जो उनके साथ नहीं मिले उन्हें प्रताड़ित किया गया। एक कर मत दो अभियान भी शुरू किया गया। 14 अप्रैल 1817 को बक्सी जगबंधु ने 5 से 10 हज़ार पाइकों और कंध जनजाति के योद्धाओं की अगवाही कर पुरी को कब्जे में ले लिया।
title: Test #12: Khurda Vidroh - 1857 Ke Bahut Pahle

text: छत्तीसगढ़ के सांस्कृतिक गौरव और सामूहिक आस्था के जीवंत प्रतीक बस्तर-दशहरा उत्सव में आकर मुझे विशेष प्रसन्नता हो रही है। प्रदेश के जनजातीय समाज में उत्सवों का महत्व जीवन के साथ गहराई से जुड़ा हुआ है। ढाई-महीने चलने वाले बस्तर-दशहरा उत्सव में समूचे समाज की जिस तरह से सहभागिता होती है, वह असाधारण है। समाज के विभिन्न वर्गों को आत्मीयता से जोड़ने वाले अनेक अनुष्ठान बस्तर-दशहरे को विशेष आकर्षक बनाते हैं। मुरिया दरबार की व्यवस्थाएं जमीन से जुड़ी लोकतान्त्रिक पद्धतियों के अच्छे उदाहरण हैं। मुरिया दरबार जैसी प्रक्रिया से प्राप्त होने वाले समाधान सबकी खुशहाली का मार्ग प्रशस्त करते हैं। इससे हमारे लोकतंत्र का गौरव बढ़ता है। बस्तर के एक प्रतिनिधिमंडल से दो माह पहले राष्ट्रपति भवन में मेरी भेंट हुई थी। इसमें बस्तर पंडुम के विजेतागण तथा बस्तर के परगना माँझी और चालकी भी शामिल थे। बस्तर पंडुम जैसे आयोजन युवाओं को अपनी परंपराओं, रीति-रिवाजों और सांस्कृतिक विरासत से पुनः जोड़ने का महत्वपूर्ण कार्य करते हैं। यह क्षेत्र दण्डकारण्य भी कहलाता है। भगवान राम के वनवास से इसका संबंध बताया जाता है। वाल्मीकि रामायण में दण्डकारण्य के रूप में जिस विशाल भूभाग का वर्णन मिलता है, उसमें आपका यह क्षेत्र भी आता है। भगवान राम की महर्षि अगस्त्य समेत अनेक ऋषियों से भेंट होने, ऋषियों और समाज को परेशान करने वाले राक्षसों का संहार करने के अनेक प्रसंग इसी दण्डकारण्य के हैं। माता सीता का अपहरण, जटायु का रावण से संघर्ष और रामजी के माता शबरी के मिलने के प्रसंग भी दण्डकारण्य से जुड़े हैं। छत्तीसगढ़ राज्य लंबे समय तक नक्सलवाद की समस्या से जूझ रहा था। केन्द्र और राज्य सरकार के समन्वित प्रयासों से नक्सली आतंक से मुक्त होकर यह क्षेत्र प्रगति के पथ पर तेजी से आगे बढ़ रहा है। मैं जनजातीय समाज से आती हूँ। देश के सुदूर अंचलों में रहने वाले समाज के इस वर्ग की अदम्य ऊर्जा और समस्याओं से मैं परिचित हूँ। उपयुक्त प्रोत्साहन मिले तो जनजातीय समाज के बेटे-बेटियाँ जीवन के हर क्षेत्र में देश का गौरव बढ़ा सकते हैं। इसके असंख्य उदाहरण आज पूरा देश देख रहा है। आज छत्तीसगढ़ के सामने विकास के अनेक द्वार खुल रहे हैं। इसके लिए मैं केन्द्र और राज्य सरकार को बधाई देती हूँ। आतंकवाद की पीड़ा को पीछे छोड़कर यह प्रदेश तीव्रता से आगे बढ़ रहा है। मुझे बताया गया है कि पिछले कुछ समय में जनजातीय उद्यमियों को वित्तीय सुविधा और बाजार से जोड़ने की पहलें और तेज की गयी हैं। मुझे विश्वास है कि समतापरक और समावेशी विकास के माध्यम से 2047 तक विकसित भारत बनाने के लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति के लिए ये कार्य उपयोगी होंगे। इस विकास यात्रा में जनजातीय समाज की प्रकृति-पोषक जीवन पद्धति से उपयोगी शिक्षा ग्रहण करनी चाहिए। मुझे बताया गया कि कल आप लोग कुटुम्ब जात्रा का आयोजन करके बस्तर दशहरा के लिए पधारे ग्राम देवी-देवताओं की श्रद्धापूर्वक विदाई करेंगे। इसके बाद 27 अक्टूबर को माँ दंतेश्वरी की पूजा-अर्चना करके उनकी और देवी मावली की डोली विदाई का आयोजन करेंगे। इन सामूहिक अनुष्ठानों को पीढ़ियों से उसी उत्साह से करते रहने की आपकी सांस्कृतिक परंपरा का मैं अभिनंदन करती हूँ। आप सबके उज्ज्वल भविष्य और छत्तीसगढ़ राज्य के तीव्र गति से समग्र विकास की मैं कामना करती हूँ। आज यहाँ आने से पहले माँझी बंधुओं से मैंने मुलाकात की। उन्होंने मुझे मुरिया दरबार की परंपरा के बारे में बताया।
title: Test #13: Bastar Dushera Ke Avsar Par Rashtrapati

text: दुनिया भर में बच्चों के लिए खिलौनों की भरमार है। व्यावसायिक दृष्टि, विचार, तकनीक और प्रबंधन ने बचपन के लिए दिलचस्प और महंगे खिलौने ईजाद किए हैं। कालक्रम में जब अभिभावक बढ़ती व्यस्तताओं के कारण बच्चों के लिए समय नहीं निकाल पाते होंगे, तो खिलौनों का जन्म हुआ होगा। इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं कि बच्चों की सीखने की क्षमता बढ़ना जरूरी है। बच्चे खिलौनों से सीखते हैं, इसलिए खिलौनों में सिखाने वाला तत्व अधिक होना चाहिए, जिससे बच्चों के भीतर कल्पना और रचनात्मकता मजबूत होती रहे। उन्हें वास्तविक ज्ञान मिलना शुरू हो, जो जिंदगी में काम आए। इससे उनका उचित शारीरिक, मानसिक और भावनात्मक विकास भी हो सकेगा। आजकल छोटे-बड़े ब्लॉक वाले जो खिलौने मिलने लगे हैं, वे बच्चों के भीतर सोचने-समझने और समस्याओं को सुलझाने की क्षमता बढ़ाते हैं। कुछ खिलौने मनोरंजन तो करते ही हैं, साथ ही दिमाग में नए विचार और नए डिजाइन भी लाते हैं। दूसरों के साथ मिलकर खेले जाने वाले खिलौने सामूहिक रूप से काम करना और संवाद करना सिखाते हैं। कल्पनाशील अभिभावक और दादा-दादी बच्चे को छड़ी पर चिपकाए कागज के कुछ फूलों से कई सप्ताह तक बहलाए रख सकते हैं। यही उसका खिलौना बना रहता है और दूसरे खिलौने अलमारी में सजे झांकते रहते हैं। पसंदीदा टेडी बियर, गुड़िया और ब्लॉक बेहद टिकाऊ और लोकप्रिय खिलौने माने जाते हैं। खिलौने सबसे पहले मिट्टी, कपड़े और लकड़ी से बनाए गए होंगे। अब तो ज्यादातर खिलौने प्लास्टिक से बनाए जा रहे हैं। लकड़ी और मिट्टी के खिलौनों का चलन बहुत कम रह गया है। सांप-सीढ़ी के खेल का आकर्षण अब भी बरकरार है। इसका कोई विकल्प नहीं। खिलौने कम और अच्छे होने चाहिए, जो बचपन में सकारात्मक भूमिका निभाएं। मगर यह तभी हो सकेगा, जब अभिभावक अपनी सुविधा और व्यस्तता के चलते बच्चों को स्मार्टफोन की आभासी दुनिया में न झोंकें। इसके बड़े खमियाजे सामने आने शुरू हो चुके हैं। बच्चों की फरमाइश, अभिभावकों, रिश्तेदारों और पारिवारिक मित्रों के कारण खिलौनों की संख्या बढ़ती रहती है। इनमें अनुपयुक्त और अवांछित खिलौने भी शामिल होते हैं। खिलौने बढ़ते जा रहे हैं। बाजार का विस्तार उनकी संख्या और किस्मों को और बढ़ाता रहेगा। साफ दिखता है कि इस मामले में सही और गलत की पहचान करने और उसके आधार पर बच्चों को खिलौनों के साथ जीना सिखाने के बारे में विचार किया जाना चाहिए। यह बात अलग है कि कई खिलौनों के डिब्बे खोलने और उनसे एक-दो बार खेलने के बाद बच्चे आमतौर पर उन्हें दोबारा देखते भी नहीं। कई खिलौने डिब्बे में बंद ही रह जाते हैं। फिर, तोहफों की दुनिया ऐसी है कि कई बार एक ही तरह के खिलौने कई जगहों से घर में आ जाते हैं। बच्चों को कुछ ही खिलौने पसंद आते हैं, जिनके साथ खेलते हुए वे अक्सर नींद में भी खो जाते हैं। इसीलिए ज्यादातर खिलौने कुछ ही समय बाद घर का उदास सामान बन जाते हैं। खिलौने बनाने वालों, बेचने वालों और अभिभावकों के पास बच्चों के लिए कम वक्त होने की मजबूरी खिलौनों की मांग बढ़ाए रखेगी। फैलती तकनीक और अब मानवीय दिमाग पर कब्जा कर रही कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता नए खिलौने बनाने के अवसर दे रही है। जिस तरह प्राकृतिक बुद्धि का कोई विकल्प नहीं, उसी तरह बचपन के आंगन में मुफ्त मिलने वाले प्राकृतिक खिलौनों या हर घर-आंगन के मौलिक, सरल और सस्ते खिलौनों का स्थान बना रहेगा। इसीलिए कुम्हार का चाक और असली मिट्टी का पैक अब भी उपलब्ध है। अनेक सार्वजनिक आयोजनों में मिट्टी के खिलौने बनाना सिखाने के लिए स्टाल लगाए जा रहे हैं। अब बहुत सारे अभिभावक सोचने लगे हैं कि उनके बच्चों का जुड़ाव प्रकृति के साथ बना रहे और उन्हें इसका फायदा मिले। बाजार और तकनीक का कब्जा जिंदगी पर कम रहे।
title: Test #14: Bachpan Mein Kyon Jaruri Hai Khilone

text: अशफाक-उल्ला खां का जन्म 22-अक्तूबर, 1900 को उत्तर-प्रदेश राज्य के शाहजहांपुर के ऐतिहासिक नगर में हुआ था। बाल्यावस्था से ही वे अत्यंत निर्भीक, साहसी, स्वाभिमानी और स्वतंत्र एवं प्रगतिशील विचारधारा वाले थे तथा रोमांचकारी घुड़सवारी, कठिन तैराकी और अचूक निशानेबाजी में विशेष अभिरुचि एवं उत्साह रखते थे। महात्मा गांधी द्वारा राष्ट्रव्यापी असहयोग आंदोलन 1922 में वापस लिए जाने के उपरांत हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन नामक क्रांतिकारी संगठन 1924 में स्थापित हुआ, जिससे अशफाक-उल्ला खां और बिस्मिल जैसे समर्पित और निष्ठावान साथी संबद्ध हुए। इसके पश्चात 1925-1927 का कालखंड क्रांतिकारियों के लिए अत्यंत कठिन, संघर्षपूर्ण और चुनौतीपूर्ण परीक्षा का दौर सिद्ध हुआ। 9-अगस्त, 1925 का काकोरी कांड भारतीय क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन का निर्णायक अध्याय बन गया। उस दिन सहारनपुर-लखनऊ रेलगाड़ी से ले जाए जा रहे ब्रिटिश सरकार के खजाने को लखनऊ के निकट काकोरी में क्रांतिकारियों ने लूट लिया। इस कार्रवाई का उद्देश्य निजी संपत्ति हथियाना नहीं बल्कि औपनिवेशिक शासन के विरुद्ध संघर्ष के लिए संसाधन जुटाना और ब्रिटिश सत्ता को चुनौती देना था। अशफाक-उल्ला खां ने इस क्रांतिकारी अभियान में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। इस घटना ने अंग्रेजी हुकूमत को झकझोर दिया और पूरे देश का ध्यान क्रांतिकारियों की ओर आकर्षित किया। अंग्रेजी शासन ने उन पर मुकद्दमा चलाया और उन्हें मृत्युदंड सुनाया। फैजाबाद जेल में 19 दिसंबर 1927 को अशफाक उल्ला खां को फांसी दे दी गई। उस समय उनकी आयु महज 27 वर्ष थी। इसी दिन राम प्रसाद बिस्मिल को गोरखपुर जेल और ठाकुर रोशन सिंह को इलाहाबाद में फांसी दी गई थी। राजेंद्रनाथ लाहिड़ी को इससे पहले 17 दिसंबर 1927 को गोंडा जेल में फांसी दी गई थी। वे जानते थे कि उनका बलिदान परिवार के लिए असहनीय पीड़ा लेकर आएगा, लेकिन मातृभूमि की स्वतंत्रता उनके लिए सर्वोपरि थी। उनकी आरजू थी कि मृत्यु के बाद उनके कफन में वतन की थोड़ी-सी मिट्टी रखी जाए। इन बलिदानों ने भारतीय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन को नई ऊर्जा दी और देश के युवाओं के विशेष प्रासंगिकता रखता है। उनकी और बिस्मिल की मित्रता सिखाती है कि देश को जोड़ने वाली सबसे बड़ी शक्ति साझा उद्देश्य और परस्पर सम्मान है।

text: Institutes of higher learning include those built by the state and by individuals of extraordinary vision. Individuals with a Big Idea. Homi J Bhabha imagined the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. J.N. Tata conceived the Indian Institute of Science. Madan Mohan Malaviya built Banaras Hindu University. Syed Ahmad Khan created Aligarh Muslim University. Bengal, too, contributed gems to this intellectual nation-building: Rabindranath Tagore’s Visva-Bharati University (1921) and P.C. Mahalanobis’s Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) (1931). If India ever declared "educational navratnas", these institutions would be among the first to qualify. Over the past decade, we have witnessed a tightening of the Union government’s control over autonomous institutions. Take the Indian Institutes of Management (IIM). The Indian Institutes of Management Act, 2017 gave them autonomy, with the power to choose their own directors and frame internal policies. However, the Indian Institutes of Management (Amendment) Act, 2023 reversed that sovereignty. Appointments of directors and key decisions must now be approved by the Ministry of Education and the President. The message was clear: Autonomy is a privilege, not a right. And it can be taken back. Or consider Visva-Bharati. Tagore built it on the ideals of openness, interdisciplinary learning, and a deep humanism. Today, that fragile ecosystem is being forced into the rigid mould of the National Education Policy, 2020. Instead of academic help, faculty are being sent for administrative training under the Rashtriya Karmayogi programme. The mantra is conforming, not flourish. The Common University Entrance Test is an example of the broader attempt to impose conformism and homogeneity. In essence, the Union government took control of who enters a university, and how. The Union government recently released the Draft Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2025 for public consultation. It proposes to transform ISI from a registered society into a statutory body, largely controlled by the Union government. The democratically structured 33-member council will be replaced by an 11-member board of governors, mostly nominated by the Union government. Clause 17 (5) says, "The Board shall, in the exercise of its power and discharge of its functions under this Act, be accountable to the Central Government." ISI is a product of the Bengal Renaissance, an era of intellectual courage, scientific rigour, and humanist values. Mahalanobis, its founder, was the architect of modern India’s statistical system. He established the National Sample Survey. His birth anniversary on 29 June is celebrated as National Statistics Day. ISI’s strength has always been its independence: An environment where statisticians, economists, computer scientists, and mathematical thinkers could work free of bureaucratic interference. That independence is now under serious threat. As the Union government attempts to bring more institutions under its direct command, one must ask: Is this really an attempt to strengthen education, or stifle it? An attempt to support institutions, or subordinate them? As a responsible Opposition, it is our duty to protect the country’s independent institutions. So, whether it is our Parliament, judiciary, Election Commission, RBI, central investigative agencies, or others, it is time we defeated all attempts to undermine them and destroy their autonomy. It is these vital institutions that protect the citizen against state power, that are empowered by the Constitution to stand as bulwarks against a rampaging executive. Above all, we need to protect our educational institutions, which have always been the first to come under attack - to indoctrinate, manipulate, control. The closing of the minds of the young has grave implications for our country’s future. India will not progress by steamrolling its institutions into identical bureaucratic units, but only when its institutions are free to think, question, innovate. Control does not create quality. Freedom does.
title: Test #01: Shifting Autonomy - One Institute at a Time

text: Century-old quantum mechanics can explain how a single sub-atomic particle cross the energy barrier through tunnelling, be located at multiple places simultaneously, occupies discrete energy levels and emits energy in quanta as it moves from higher energy level to lower energy level. Three US Physics Professors; were awarded this year’s Physics Nobel Prize. Quantum mechanics has advanced from single particle to macroscopic level, and during 1984 and 1985 these Professors have conducted experiments wherein quantum behavior has been observed at the macroscopic level, where billions and trillions of Cooper particles (two-electron closed system) are involved. The Professors had discovered macroscopic mechanical tunneling and quantized energy level in a system large enough to be kept in hand. The quantum behavior in superconducting circuits has led to the creation of superconducting qubits, the building blocks of quantum computers and can perform intricate calculations far beyond the reach of a classical computer, marking the dawn of a new computational era. Google Sycamore processor, co-developed by martinis has already demonstrated quantum supremacy by solving problems faster than any existing supercomputer. The implications extend far beyond computing. When they made this discovery in 1984 and 1985, Martinis was a PhD candidate, Devoret was a postdoctoral fellow, and Clarke was their professor and supervisor. Two of the three Laureates have links with Google. Besides his professorship Devoret, is Chief Scientist of Google Quantum AI, while Martinis headed Google’s Quantum AI lab till 2020. How Quantum Mechanics is different from Classical Mechanics? We have seen in our day today life that when a ball is thrown against a wall, it rebounds on the same side and never crosses to the other side of the wall. In sharp contrast to this, atomic particles under quantum mechanical principles cross the barrier through tunneling, located at multiple positions simultaneously and can occupy discrete energy levels. In 1973 Physics Nobel Prize was won by Brian Josephson for discovering the flow of electric current between two superconductors separated by an insulator. This has been a very useful finding and superconductor-insulator-superconductor junction has been used in various experiments like measurement of fundamental physical constants and magnetic field etc. and is commonly called as Josephson junction. This set-up was utilized by Nobel Laureates in the series of experiments they conducted in 1984 and 1985 meticulously isolated the set-up from its environment and ensured that the quantum effects are not destroyed by interference. They were successful in demonstrating the flow of electron through the set-up and also found the electrons exhibiting quantum mechanical behavior. The superconducting chip separating another superconductor by an insulator had electric current flowing without any resistance. The electrons coordinate and move together in a single wave. The voltmeter reading showing zero initially starts showing value corresponding to a discrete energy level confirming that the particle has crossed the wall (the insulator) through tunneling. Though the scientists have not been able to conclude the maximum size of the system exhibiting the quantum behavior, but the experiments conducted in 1984 and 1985 by the Nobel Laureates have confirmed that the system as large as the set-up chosen by them did show quantum behavior. The discovery led to the building of quantum-bits (qubits) unit of information in quantum computers. The discovery has been extensively used in mobiles, cameras, transistors in computer microchips and optic cables etc. that are part of our lives these days. The next generation quantum technology such as quantum cryptography, quantum computers and quantum sensors are the way forward from these inventions. These discoveries have far reaching consequences and have been providing breakthroughs in many fields of medicine, chemistry and environment etc.
title: Test #02: Physics Nobel Prize - Quantum Computing is the Future

text: IN WORLD health statistics, the burden of polluted air keeps increasing each year, and AQI reports continuously warn about the rising concentration of toxic particles suspended in the atmosphere. Countries like India and Pakistan face repeated environmental emergencies whenever particulate matter becomes extremely dense during winter months, especially in urban centers that already struggle with traffic congestion and industrial smoke. This hazardous situation affects school-going children, elderly citizens, and millions of people who already suffer from asthma or other breathing disorders, making everyday life extremely difficult for them. Moreover, severe pollution reduces visibility, slows transportation, and forces several cities to close educational institutions for safety reasons. In many regions, AQI levels go beyond the "Severe" category, which means even healthy individuals may experience burning eyes, coughing, or excessive fatigue while staying outdoors. India’s capital region and Pakistan’s Lahore are repeatedly listed among the most polluted places during global surveys, raising international concern about long-term environmental consequences. Scientists argue that without strict emission control, renewable energy policies, and large-scale public awareness, the regional air quality will continue to decline, eventually causing major health crises and economic losses. Ultimately, saving the environment must become a shared responsibility for citizens, industries, and both governments, because clean air is not a luxury-it is a basic requirement for human survival. With Asia having experienced the most dramatic episodes of air pollution in recent years, many studies have focused on regional solutions. In 2016, the Climate and Clean Air Coalition commissioned a report to find solutions to air pollution in Indian cities. The report Breathing Cleaner Air: Ten Scalable Solutions for Indian Cities was led by a task force of Indian and international experts. It outlined solutions that can significantly reduce air pollution in the country, including preventing agricultural open burning by turning crop residue into a resource to produce fuel for electricity generation. A similar report focusing on regional solutions was published by UNEP and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition last year called Air Pollution in Asia and the Pacific: Science-based Solutions, detailing 25 policy and technological measures that will deliver benefits across sectors. It represented the first comprehensive scientific assessment of the air pollution outlook in Asia and the Pacific and highlighted that adopting the 25 recommended measures could lead to a reduction in premature mortality in the region by one third, helping to avoid 2 million premature deaths from indoor air pollution per year. Reports converge on the finding that local governments must play a central role in the fight to BeatAirPollution in the region. Jambi City, which received international media attention due to its sky turning red during the latest crisis in Indonesia, has approved an emissions mitigation plan that includes reducing and capturing methane from waste, local regulations that ban waste burning and planting trees to make its neighbourhoods greener. Having recently joined the BreatheLife network, it is but one example of how cities are taking the lead in Asia to improve air quality and protect their citizens and our planet. Furthermore, this year the Indian government joined the Climate and Clean Air Coalition on the occasion of World Environment Day. India’s Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Prakash Javadekar, stated then that India will work to "adopt cleaner energy, sustainable production and consumption patterns" as well as "environment-friendly transport, agriculture, industry and waste management to promote clean air". The UN Environment Assembly, together with other global entities, has called for heightened action to improve air quality and to address pollution in general.
title: Test #03: World Level Air Pollution & AQI Report

text: OpenAI is an advanced artificial intelligence company that began with one clear idea: powerful AI should help all of humanity, not just a small group; this simple but bold purpose has guided the organization since the day it was created! Many people ask: What exactly does OpenAI do? The answer is both simple and deep, because OpenAI builds AI models that can understand language, solve problems, create images, write code, and even help in scientific research. But the company does not just build tools, it also studies how to make AI safe, fair, and useful, because without safety, even the smartest machine can cause trouble. OpenAI believes that technology should be developed with great care; this is why the company spends so much time testing, reviewing, and improving its models, almost like a teacher checking every lesson again and again. If someone asks, “Why is OpenAI famous?” the reply is clear: it created powerful models like ChatGPT, which can talk, explain, imagine, and assist millions of users every day! These tools may look magical, but behind them stand years of research, large teams, and strong values that keep everything balanced and responsible. One special thing about OpenAI is its focus on alignment, which means the AI must behave in a way that matches human values such as honesty, safety, fairness, and kindness. This idea sounds simple, but making it work in real life is a huge challenge that the company takes very seriously. Alignment requires constant observation, learning, and correction, ensuring that AI remains a partner to humans rather than a problem. People often worry: will AI replace jobs or control humans? OpenAI gives a balanced reply. AI will replace some tasks, but it will also create new jobs and new opportunities, and humans will always be needed for creativity, judgment, and emotional understanding! This way of thinking helps remove fear and encourages people to use AI as a tool rather than see it as an enemy. Even in industries like education, healthcare, customer service, and research, AI acts more like an assistant than a master, lifting the burden of repetitive tasks and allowing humans to focus on thoughtful and meaningful work. Another strong part of OpenAI’s mission is openness: the company shares research papers, safety updates, and useful guides so that the world can understand how AI works; this helps build trust, especially in a time when technology is growing faster than ever. Still, OpenAI knows that speed must be balanced with responsibility; for this reason, it performs careful testing, sets rules for usage, and allows experts to examine risks before releasing any major model. The company also collaborates with teachers, students, developers, and businesses so that AI can support education, medicine, science, and creativity—fields that directly touch human life. It is inspiring to see how OpenAI keeps improving: each new model becomes more accurate, more helpful, more aware of context, and more capable of understanding human intention. This progress makes it easier for users to learn, explore, solve problems, and grow; yet the company never forgets that power must come with wisdom! OpenAI also studies how to reduce bias, prevent harmful actions, and ensure that AI stays a force for good. Bias is a major issue in technology, and OpenAI spends enormous effort on audits, evaluations, and continuous refinement. This careful balance of progress and caution makes it different from many other tech companies. While others may focus only on speed, OpenAI tries to balance speed with ethics, creativity with responsibility, and innovation with safety. The company also invests in long-term research: how will AI behave in complex situations? How can it understand subtle human emotions? How can it avoid misinterpretation? These are not simple questions, and solving them requires scientists, philosophers, engineers, and policy experts working together. OpenAI encourages this teamwork because AI is not just a technical challenge-it is a human challenge.
title: Test #04: Why is Open AI Famous?

text: Artificial intelligence, often called AI, has quickly changed the way humans think, work, and create, yet many people still wonder: what exactly gives AI its power? At its core, AI is the science of building systems that can “learn” from data, notice patterns, and make decisions, sometimes faster, sometimes better, then humans! OpenAI, a leading research group in this field, believes that AI should help everyone, not just a few, and this idea shapes the tools it builds, from language models to robots and safety systems. But the story does not end there. In fact, it only begins, because AI is not simply a machine that answers questions, it is a mirror that shows our strengths, weaknesses, and imagination. When a student asks, “Can AI help me understand the world better?” the answer is yes, but with care. AI gives information, yet the responsibility to think clearly remains with the human being. Think about how OpenAI trains its models: by giving them huge amounts of text, correcting mistakes, and enforcing safety rules, much like a teacher guiding a curious child. However, unlike a child, AI does not feel anything, which is both a strength and a limit. This emotionless clarity allows AI to handle very large amounts of data without getting tired, confused, or emotional, but it also means humans must judge its answers wisely, especially when the results look too confident or too perfect! Interestingly, OpenAI focuses strongly on alignment, meaning the AI should act in ways that are helpful, honest, and safe. This idea may sound simple, yet applying it needs great effort, because human values are complex, changing, and sometimes even opposite. Another deep question comes up: will AI replace people? The honest answer is that AI will replace tasks, not the human spirit, because creativity, intuition, and moral judgment belong only to us, no matter how advanced a model becomes. Instead of fighting with AI, OpenAI encourages teamwork, where humans use AI as a tool to grow their ability to write, solve problems, and explore new ideas. In this way, technology becomes a partner rather than a danger, a guide rather than a competitor. Still, problems exist: misinformation, misuse, and bias can spread quickly if AI is not trained and checked well. Therefore, OpenAI spends a lot on safety research, clear reports, and strict testing, all of which help people trust the technology more. Safety teams examine worst-case scenarios, evaluate how models respond under pressure, and fix failures before they reach the public. Such work is slow, careful, and sometimes invisible, yet it is the backbone of responsible AI. The real magic of AI lies not in replacing humans but in helping us ask better questions, questions like: “How can we use intelligence, whether natural or artificial, to reduce suffering, improve education, and increase understanding?” Such questions remind us that progress is not automatic. It is a choice, guided by curiosity and responsibility. AI can shine light on patterns, but only humans can decide what to do with that light. OpenAI often says that AI is a tool for expanding human potential. A writer uses it to break creative blocks, a scientist uses it to test hypotheses, a teacher uses it to explain concepts more clearly. Yet none of these achievements remove the essential role of human wisdom. AI may accelerate thinking, but it cannot replace reflection; it can reveal options, but it cannot determine purpose. Even more interesting is how AI pushes humans to understand themselves more deeply. When a model makes a mistake, we learn where our instructions were unclear. When it succeeds, we learn how structure, clarity, and logic can elevate communication. In this way, AI becomes both a companion and a challenge, urging us to refine our thinking. Yet, as with all powerful tools, caution remains essential. AI can unintentionally repeat biases found in its training data, produce misleading answers, or be misused by irresponsible actors.
title: Test #05: AI is the Science of Building System

text: Michael Faraday was an English scientist who made important contributions to the fields of electrochemistry and electromagnetism. The concepts underlying electromagnetic induction, diamagnetism, and electrolysis were among his most important discoveries. Despite his lack of formal education, Faraday was one of the most prominent scientists in history. Faraday provided the foundation for the idea of the electromagnetic field in physics through his experiments on the magnetic field around a conductor holding a direct current. Faraday also discovered that magnetism could influence light rays and that the two phenomena had an underlying relationship. He also discovered the rules of electrolysis and the concepts of electromagnetic induction and diamagnetism. His electromagnetic rotary system designs laid the groundwork for electric motor technology, and it was because of his efforts that electricity became useful in technology. Faraday was an excellent experimenter who communicated his ideas in simple language; however, his mathematical skills were limited to the simplest algebra. Michael Faraday was born on September 22, 1791, in Newington Butts, a Surrey suburb that is now part of the London Borough of Southwark. His family did not have a lot of income. James, his father, belonged to the Glassite Christian sect. During the winter of 1790, James Faraday moved his wife and two children from Outhgill, Westmorland, to London, where he had worked as an apprentice to the village blacksmith. In the autumn of that year, Michael was born. Michael Faraday, the third of four brothers, had to educate himself after receiving only a basic school education. Faraday's work on electricity and magnetism is what he is best known for. The creation of a voltaic pile of seven British halfpenny coins, seven discs of sheet zinc, and six pieces of paper moistened with salt water was his first known experiment. He broke down the sulphate of magnesia with this pile. Faraday continued his laboratory work after his initial observation in 1821, investigating the electromagnetic properties of materials and gaining the necessary knowledge. Faraday set up a circuit in 1824 to see whether a magnetic field could influence current flow in an adjacent wire, but he found no such relationship. This experiment followed three years of related experiments with light and magnets, which yielded identical results. Faraday spent the next seven years perfecting his formula for optical consistency (heavy) glass, borosilicate of lead, which he would later use in his experiments linking light and magnetism. Faraday used "static," batteries, and "animal electricity" to generate the phenomenon of electrostatic attraction, electrolysis, magnetism, and other phenomena in 1832, as part of a series of experiments aimed at determining the fundamental essence of electricity. He concluded that contrary to popular belief at the time, the distinctions between different "kinds" of electricity were illusory. Instead, Faraday suggested that there is only one "electricity," and that differing quantities and intensities (current and voltage) generate various classes of phenomena. Faraday discovered in 1845 that certain materials had a mild repulsion to a magnetic field, which he called diamagnetism. Faraday also discovered that by applying an external magnetic field aligned with the direction in which the light is travelling, the plane of polarization of linearly polarised light can be rotated. The Faraday effect is the name given to this phenomenon. "I have at last succeeded in lighting a magnetic curve or line of force and in magnetising a beam of light," he wrote in his notebook in September 1845. Faraday began his chemistry career as a chemist's assistant to Humphry Davy. Faraday was particularly interested in the study of chlorine, and he found two new chlorine-carbon compounds. He also carried out the first rudimentary experiments on gas diffusion, which was first observed by John Dalton. Faraday was active in liquefying several gases, researching steel alloys, and producing several new forms of optical glass.
title: Test #06: Michael Faraday Scientist & His Work

text: In 2022, Dr. Gurumukhi launched one of the most ambitious educational development programs aimed at transforming the way rural and semi-urban communities accessed digital knowledge. Recognizing the widening gap between technologically advanced cities and resource-limited villages, The designed a comprehensive model that blended digital tools, offline support, and community participation. Under his guidance, a series of Digital Learning Resource Centers were established, each equipped with computers, tablets, projectors, and reliable internet connectivity. These centers became hubs where students, teachers, and even elderly residents could explore new skills at their own pace. As part of this initiative, Dr. Gurumukhi developed specialized training modules tailored to different age groups. School children were introduced to interactive learning apps, while college-going youth were offered career-oriented courses such as computer programming, financial literacy, and communication skills. Farmers received digital training to help them access crop advisories, market prices, and government schemes more efficiently. Women from self-help groups were also encouraged to participate, gaining exposure to online entrepreneurship and digital banking. As the program expanded, Dr. Gurumukhi realized that access alone was not enough; people also needed confidence in using technology for everyday tasks. To address this, he introduced a system of Digital Mentors—trained volunteers from local colleges who regularly visited villages to guide learners, troubleshoot basic technical issues, and encourage hesitant users to adopt the new tools. Their presence created a bridge between first-time learners and unfamiliar technologies, ensuring that no one felt left behind during the transition. These mentors became role models for younger children, demonstrating how digital literacy could open pathways to academic and professional success. In collaboration with district authorities, he also initiated community awareness drives highlighting the importance of cybersecurity, responsible online behaviour, and safe digital practices. Sessions on password protection, identifying fraudulent messages, avoiding misinformation, and understanding online privacy were conducted in simple, relatable language. This helped residents, especially the elderly and less educated groups, to participate confidently in the digital space without fear of manipulation or misuse. As part of the broader digital vision, the program integrated several national initiatives such as DigiLocker, Aadhaar-enabled services, UPI payments, and the Digital India framework. Local kiosks were set up to help residents access important certificates, land records, identity documents, and benefit schemes through online portals. This significantly reduced dependence on intermediaries and eliminated many long-standing delays associated with paper-based processes. For many villagers, completing tasks in minutes—tasks that once took entire days—became a moment of empowerment. The digital centers also hosted monthly innovation workshops where students worked on small projects like basic coding exercises, data entry simulations, mobile photography, and content creation. These activities nurtured creativity and inspired learners to explore digital careers they had never previously imagined. Teachers received training in creating digital lesson plans, using virtual classrooms, and adopting blended-learning methods that combined textbooks with multimedia content. This boosted classroom engagement and improved overall learning outcomes. To support agriculture and rural livelihoods, the program partnered with expert institutions to introduce farmers to satellite-based weather updates, soil testing apps, and online marketplaces. This helped them make informed decisions, reduce crop losses, and negotiate better prices. Women entrepreneurs, meanwhile, learned to promote their products on social media, manage online orders, and leverage digital payment platforms.
title: Test #07: Dr. Gurumukhi & Digital India - UPSSSC 27th 1st

text: A planetarium is a scientific theatre where people can explore the universe without leaving the Earth. It is a unique place that brings the wonders of space closer to everyone. Many countries including India the United States of America Japan Australia Canada Germany and France have developed advanced planetariums that help visitors understand the mysteries hidden in the vast sky. These places play an important role in encouraging curiosity and learning among students’ researchers and space enthusiasts. Inside a large dome shaped hall, a powerful digital projector creates a realistic view of the night sky. Thousands of stars glowing planets and distant galaxies appear as if they are floating above the audience. The experience often feels so real that people forget they are sitting inside a theatre. Modern planetariums also use high quality sound systems and animated visuals to explain complex scientific ideas in simple and engaging ways. Visitors can learn about the formation of stars the movement of planets and the possibility of life on other worlds. Shows in a planetarium also highlight space missions’ telescopes and discoveries made by astronomers. Many planetariums conduct workshops exhibitions and educational programs for children which help them develop an interest in science and technology. A visit to a planetarium is not only educational but also inspiring. It encourages people to look up at the sky with wonder and think about the endless universe. Usually, the projection theatre of those kinds of planetariums can be 82 feet or 25 meters in diameter. The capacities of these planetariums can exceed over 600 people. On the other hand, when it comes to local college or community planetariums, those spaces are only able to accommodate small-groups of people. There is also a separate class of portable planetariums that consist of inflatable domes and lightweight projectors. The domes and projectors can be set up at school to hold several students at the same time. It should also be noted that a projection instrument is vital for every great planetarium. That being said, the first modern electromechanical planetarium projector was built by Carl Zeiss, which was a German optical firm, in 1923. This projector was used in the Deutsches Museum in Munich. The current versions of this instrument are more technically complex, controlled by computer combinations, uses motor drives, fibre-optics, lenses, lamps, and other devices that help in designing the place of the planets, the sun, and the moon in their correct locations. Some devices also help in allocating the position of thousands of stars for hundreds and thousands of years. There are also other instruments that can add several details like the Milky Way, horizon scenes, comets, nebulae, meteors, reference lines, and scales. These features can be used for celestial navigation and descriptive astronomy. These days planetariums that are based out of institutions are replacing and complementing electromechanical projectors with other technologies. This includes all-digital projector systems that are equipped with fish-eye lenses. These planetariums also come with laser projection systems that can scan the image on the screen by using colour-controlled laser beams. A seamless blending of images of the sky, artwork, videos, photos, and animations generated by the computer can also be accomplished by using digital and laser systems. These devices can also stimulate accurate views from any particular perspective in space. It also takes viewers on a virtual flight that goes beyond the solar system and into interstellar and intergalactic space. There are other variations of the screen configurations and seating arrangements that are quite common. These configurations can range from the traditional horizontal domed screen to concentric seating that is located around a central projector for distorted or tilted domes. This is also present in auditorium seating and wraparound screens.
title: Test #08: What is Planetarium - UPSSSC 27th 2nd

text: The Bay of Bengal plays a significant role in shaping the natural environment and cultural identity of the eastern coastline of India. Stretching along this vast water body is the city of Visakhapatnam, often admired for its scenic beaches, naval base, and growing industrial importance. The coastal area surrounding the city is known for its pleasant climate, rolling hills, and long stretches of golden sand that attract visitors from across the country. What makes this region truly unique is the harmonious blend of languages and cultures found among its people. Communities living here speak Telugu, Odia, Bengali, Tamil, and several tribal dialects, reflecting centuries of migration and cultural exchange. The traditions, festivals, music, and cuisine of the coastal population showcase a rich heritage shaped by both the sea and the surrounding landscape. Fishing remains one of the oldest and most important occupations in this belt. Early in the morning, fishermen set out into the Bay of Bengal with their colorful boats, returning later with fresh catch that supports local markets and industries. Alongside them, modern development has brought educational institutions, ports, shipyards, and technology centers, turning Visakhapatnam into a dynamic urban hub. Despite rapid progress, the people of the coastal region maintain a deep connection with nature. They celebrate festivals dedicated to the sea, respect coastal ecosystems, and continue practices that have been passed down through generations. This blend of tradition and modernity makes the coastline of the Bay of Bengal a vibrant example of India’s cultural diversity. region truly unique is the harmonious blend of languages and cultures found among its people. The Bay of Bengal plays an important role in sustaining agriculture in the region. In India and Bangladesh, agriculture heavily depends on monsoon rainfall, which is largely influenced by the south-eastern winds from the bay. The river deltas draining into the bay create fertile plains that support a variety of crops, including rice, wheat, maize, sugarcane, jute, and oilseeds. Additionally, the bay’s coastal waters facilitate aquaculture, including fish, shrimp, and crab farming, which is a major source of income for local communities. The consistent water supply from rivers and rainfall ensures irrigation for millions of hectares, making the bay region a vital contributor to national food security. The Bay of Bengal regulates regional climate by moderating temperatures and facilitating monsoon patterns. Warm surface waters store heat, which interacts with monsoon winds, river runoff, ocean currents, and evaporation to influence precipitation, humidity, and temperature across South and Southeast Asia. By distributing heat and moisture, the bay provides more stable weather conditions, preventing extreme heat events and supporting agricultural productivity. The Bay of Bengal acts as a natural barrier against invasions from the east, complementing India’s mountainous northern boundaries.

text: In 2022 Jalpaiguri and Puttaparthi were discussed for their peaceful surroundings and growing regional importance. Jalpaiguri was known for its green tea gardens calm lifestyle and wide natural landscape that attracted visitors from many places. People from nearby areas often visited the town for trade and daily needs and the local markets supported the economy of the district. On the other hand, Puttaparthi in the southern region was known for its simple environment and spiritual atmosphere. Many people travelled there to experience its calm setting and to take part in social and cultural activities. Both Jalpaiguri and Puttaparthi showed how different parts of the country offered unique qualities. One was known for natural beauty and agriculture while the other was known for peace culture and community life. Their steady development in 2022 highlighted the role of small towns in shaping social and economic progress. Jalpaiguri’s tea estates, such as Jayanti Tea Garden, Jalpaiguri Tea Garden, and Gopaldhara Tea Estate, drew travelers seeking serenity amid lush greenery and mountain views, boosting tea tourism alongside wildlife safaris in areas like Gorumara National Park and Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary. These attractions, enriched by rivers like Teesta and Jaldhaka, supported local economies through nature-based activities and preserved cultural sites like Jalpesh Temple and Rajbari Palace. Meanwhile, Puttaparthi’s Prasanthi Nilayam ashram, established in 1950, continued to magnetize global pilgrims for meditation, prayer, and service projects, even post-2011, fostering sustainable spiritual tourism with sites like Chaitanya Jyoti Museum. Small towns like these exemplified India’s broader shift, where Tier 2 and 3 areas contributed around 40% to national GDP by enhancing infrastructure, skill hubs, and employment in tourism and agriculture. In northern regions, Dooars tea gardens addressed challenges through government-backed tea tourism initiatives, improving worker incomes and reducing migration pressures. Southern spiritual centers like Puttaparthi evolved volunteer-driven humanitarian efforts, blending peace with community upliftment amid rising visitor infrastructure. This growth mirrored trends in other small towns, such as Atchutapuram and Kavuru, which became employment magnets via industries, easing urban migration and empowering locals. Enhanced connectivity—roads, rails, and airports—spurred housing sales up 20% and retail expansion, transforming modest locales into vibrant hubs. Jalpaiguri’s forests and ethnic villages complemented Puttaparthi’s global harmony ethos, proving small towns drive inclusive progress through unique natural and cultural assets. By 2022, such developments underscored policy focus on AMRUT and Smart Cities missions, amplifying small-town roles in social cohesion and economic resilience across diverse landscapes. Jalpaiguri benefits from projects under Dooars Mega Project, including eco-cottages at Damdim, Chamurchi, and homestays per West Bengal policy, alongside Gorumara and Jaldapara reserves. These draw eco-tourists year-round, peaking November-April, with rivers like Teesta enhancing appeal. Puttaparthi centers on spiritual sites like Chaitanya Jyoti Museum and the ashram, attracting pilgrims for meditation despite reduced global draw since 2011. Recent tourism in Jalpaiguri has shown stronger momentum driven by nature and wildlife attractions in the Dooars region, while Puttaparthi experiences steady but more niche spiritual visitation posts its founder's passing. West Bengal anticipates 25-40% growth in tourist traffic for FY 2024-25 and 2025-26, benefiting Jalpaiguri through enhanced connectivity and marketing for tea gardens and forests. Puttaparthi, within Anantapur district, relies on Prasanthi Nilayam's enduring appeal amid Andhra Pradesh's broader tourism recovery, though specific growth lags behind high-profile sites like Tirupati. Jalpaiguri edges ahead in diversified growth via government initiatives, contrasting Puttaparthi's specialized spiritual niche.

text: Delhi is in the spotlight once again for its consistently deteriorating AQI levels. And like every year there has only been a knee-jerk reaction to the problem, rather than a sustainable solution. The Commission for Air Quality Management has gradually switched from stage-1 and 2 to stage-3 of the Graded Response Action Plan, and advisories have been issued for citizens who battle serious health risks. However, there is a dire need to understand the collusion of natural and man-made reasons for air pollution, for Delhi’s air pollution crisis goes beyond India’s sovereign borders. What is happening in South Asia? In November 2024, eastern and northern Pakistan and north India faced a severe pollution event that came to be known as the ‘2024 India-Pakistan Smog’. Lahore and Delhi virtually competed on the scale of the most polluted city with the highest AQI reading globally. ‘Brown clouds’ formed in swathes over the cities distinctly visible in satellite images. While Lahore was faced with the worst AQI, Delhi’s air gradually deteriorated due to a shift in wind patterns that carried pollutants across borders and within the region. Now in 2025, Delhi is once again followed by Lahore. The Dawn from Karachi reported that local pollution and smoke drifted in from India due to low-speed winds. Bangladesh also has a significant share in the air pollution crisis. Dhaka is witnessing worsening AQI in the range from moderate to very poor during the winter season, as reported by the U.S. thinktank Atlantic Council. Likewise, in the capital of Nepal, AQI remains alarmingly high every year, between moderate and unhealthy. What are the reasons? The Greenpeace 2023 World Air Quality Report underlined that poor air quality in South Asia is due to anthropogenic sources such as industrial and vehicular emissions, and burning of solid fuel and wastages. The shared air pollution across the Indo-Gangetic Plain and beyond, with tier-1 cities facing the consequences, can be accounted by for factors such as the fixed topography of the region. Although separated by cartography, the regional topography of South Asia causes fixed ventilation of natural air and dispersal of pollutants. A trans-national and regional haze surfaces due to the complex composition of air particulates. Alongside the natural geography, there is a transnational and regional commonality - the failure in managing such crises due to abysmal political will. The World Bank report on ‘Air Pollution and Public Health in South Asia’ in 2023 informed that nine out of the world’s 10 cities with the worst air pollution are in South Asia. Sri Lanka, Maldives and Bhutan are known to be relatively less affected by transregional air pollution in the region of South Asia. This interplay of factors shows that mitigation requires attention to not only short-term solutions but also long-term strategies that focus on strong decarbonisation measures and structural reforms in agricultural practices and industry emissions across national borders. Is this a crisis of development? Air pollution is related to larger issues of development and its adverse consequences for the environment. A World Bank study estimates that high AQI levels in India results in about 3% of its GDP being spent on healthcare and lost labour capital. The Lancet Health Journal highlighted that in 2019 India’s GDP reduced by 1.36% due to premature morbidity and mortality as a result of air pollution. A steep rise in the sale of automobile vehicles, lack of public transport, negligible support for non-vehicular mobility, and building concrete structures at the expense of urban greenery are some of the reasons which lead to deteriorating air quality. text: When Charles Darwin was born in 1809 science was still in its baby shoes. Chemists were talking about atoms, physicists about energy and electricity. Nobody really knew what it was. By the time he died in 1882 scientists were able to explain light and electromagnetic waves. And, thanks to Darwin, biologists were able to explain how life on Earth developed. Darwin was the best biologist of all times. He was an expert on plants, animals and insects. But he didn’t want to be a biologist at first. At school and the university Darwin was just an average student. He read a lot and collected beetles and butterflies. He went to Edinburgh to study medicine but soon found out that it wasn’t the right thing for him. At Cambridge he met a fellow botanist, John Steven Henslow. Henslow helped him get a job on the exploration ship Beagle. The ship travelled around the world for five years and Darwin learned a lot about the forms of life. When Darwin returned to England he was a well-known scientist who lived an isolated life in the countryside where he did experiments and studied plants and animals. Darwin read a lot of interesting books. One of them influenced him a great deal. A popular economist claimed that when the population grew the people would need more and more food. But there was not enough for everybody, so food would become scarce and not everyone could survive and have children. Darwin thought that this had to be true for animals and plants as well. Those that had food would survive and the others would die. This helped Darwin solve many questions of life. While many scientists thought that all animals and plants had always been the same Darwin wasn’t sure about this. During his voyage on the Beagle he began to think about it. He explored places where he saw that many animals and plants were similar, but in a way, they were different too. Some of these differences were good and helped animals survive. They passed these on to their offspring. Darwin proved that species could change. We humans have some features from our parents, but we also have others, maybe better ones as well. We will probably pass on these better features to our children. The same works in the world of animals and plants. As time goes on species change completely, sometimes slowly, at other times quite fast. His book On the Origin of Species explained how species change. Many people didn’t like it because it had many totally new ideas. But today almost all scientists agree with Darwin’s ideas. They have continued work on his basic ideas and observe how life develops. Why do human beings look a bit like monkey or apes? Why are dolphins’ good swimmers? Why do giraffes have long necks? The answer to all these questions is evolution. Evolution is the way life changes through time. All living things are connected together like branches in a tree. Plants and animals are related to one another through their ancestors. For example, we share a common ancestor with gorillas, dogs or even mushrooms. Evolution shows us how and why all living things change over a certain period of time. We cannot watch changes in life directly. They take place over thousands or millions of years. However, scientists cannot find proof that these changes have taken place. Important evidence for evolution comes from fossils, the leftovers of ancient life. When animals or plants die they are pressed into sand or clay. Over millions of years rocks are formed. Scientists have found out that different fossils are found in rocks of different ages. For example, the oldest rocks of our earth are about 3.8 billion years old. They contain no fossils because there was probably no life at that time. Fossils of bacteria appear in rocks that are about 3.5 billion years old. Fish, reptile and mammal fossils appear in younger rocks. Human fossils are found only in the youngest and highest rock layers. Fossils also show that certain groups of animals have evolved from other groups. Amphibians evolved from fish that could breathe air and move on land.
title: Test #12: Charles Darwin - Theory of Evolution

Sir, our Government was the first ever to set up a separate Ministry of Panchayati Raj. The Minister for Panchayati Raj has been passionately committed to the empowerment of Panchayats with the aim to realizing Mahatma Gandhi dream of Poorna Swaraj through Gram Swaraj. This Report is a measure of the successes we have achieved so far and the road we still have to travel. Sir, I am very happy to be here today when the issue of Panchayati Raj and its progress is being discussed. I believe the Ministry has compiled a Report on the state of the Panchayats. I hope, States and Union Territories will soon follow with their respective reports. It is important that its achievements and shortcomings be appraised on the basis of objective data and scientific evaluation. When this report is released in the Parliament, hopefully there will be a serious debate on the state of local self-government in our country. Sir, the task that remains is to transform the political and social empowerment that we have achieved through Panchayati Raj into effective administrative and economic empowerment. This is still to happen in many States. The National Common Minimum Programme stresses that effective devolution of functions, finances and functionaries. It is only when these come together that Panchayats will be truly empowered to fulfill their mandated role. To this end, I believe, three critical steps are necessary. Firstly, the key to the effective devolution of functions is the Activity Map. Every State must prepare a detailed Activity Map that clearly spells out the activity in respect of each devolved function that must be carried out at each of the levels of our three tier system of Panchayati Raj. I am happy to learn that State Panchayati Raj Ministers have jointly agreed that Activity Maps be prepared on the principle of subsidiarity. Any activity which can be carried out at a lower level must be entrusted to that level. Equally, Ministries at the Centre also need to prepare Activity Maps. Secondly, to secure effective devolution of Finances, budgets of all line departments must open a Panchayat sector window through which Panchayats have the necessary financial resources to undertake the duties entrusted to them. The best Panchayati Raj States have already opened such windows. I hope other States will follow. Thirdly, the Approach Paper to the Eleventh Five Year Plan stresses the importance of grassroots planning. The Planning Commission has issued guidelines to all States to base their annual and five year perspective plans on district plans prepared in conformity which Constitutional provisions. Sir, the experience with Panchayats and their role and status varies from one region to another. The Report highlights the lack of basic resources and facilities, etc. in many Panchayats. States must learn from each other on effective empowerment of Panchayats. Panchayat functionaries need continuous training and capacity building.

text: Though, therefore, you may not be able to derive as much advantage from a study of the French system of constituent law as that of the Swiss that is no reason why you should not seek to derive what advantage you can in the preparation of the task before you, by a study of it. As a matter of fact, the French constitution makers, who met in 1789 at the first Constituent Assembly of their country, were themselves largely influenced by the work done but a couple of years earlier in 1787, by the historic Constitutional Convention held by the American constitution makers, for their country. Having thrown off their allegiance to the British King in Parliament, they met and drew up what had been regarded, and justly so, as the soundest, and most practical and workable republican constitution in existence. It is this great constitution, which had been naturally taken as the model for all subsequent constitutions not only of France, but also of the self-governing Dominions of the British Commonwealth, like Canada, Australia, and South Africa and I have no doubt that you will also, in the nature of things, pay in the course of your work, greater attention to the provisions of the American Constitution than to those of any other. I have referred above to the self-governing constitutions of the great Dominions of the British Commonwealth being based on, to a large extent, if not actually derived, from, the American constitutional system. The first to benefit by the American system was Canada, the historic Convention of which country, for drawing up a self- governing constitution, met in 1864. This Convention drew up the Canadian Constitution, which was subsequently embodied in what is still on the Statute Book as the British North American Act, passed by the British Parliament in 1867. You may be interested to hear that the said Convention consisted of only 33 delegates from all the provinces of Canada, and that Convention of 33 representatives issued as many as 74 resolutions, which were afterwards duly incorporated in toto in the British North American Act, under the provisions of which the first self-governing Dominion of the British Commonwealth of Canada, came into existence, in 1867. The British Parliament accepted tile Canadian Convention scheme in its entirety, except for making only one drafting amendment. I hope and pray, Hon'ble Members, that your labours may be crowned with a similar success. The American constitutional system was more or less adopted in the schemes prepared for framing the Constitutions of Australia and South Africa, which shows that the results achieved by the American Convention held in 1787, had been accepted by the world as a model for framing independent federal constitutions for various countries. It is for these reasons that I have felt justified in inviting your attention to the American system of constituent and constitutional law as one which should be carefully studied by you not necessarily for wholesale adoption, but for the judicious adaptation of its provisions.
title: Test #16: SSC Special Passage - Study of the French System
