Nordic and Scandinavian education systems, some tracing reform efforts back to the period 1967-1978, increasingly integrate emotional well-being, social-emotional learning, digital citizenship, anti-bullying efforts, outdoor activity, and parent-school collaboration into routine schooling. India now needs a similar, sustained societal response. Families must practise more active parenting not surveillance or constant correction, but genuine connection. Teachers and parents must share observations systematically, because teachers may notice changes in concentration or friendship patterns long before parents do, while parents may detect disturbed sleep or emotional withdrawal before any teacher can. Such partnerships are no longer optional; they are essential infrastructure for modern childhood. Adolescents aged 6 to 17 are facing emotional and behavioural challenges earlier, faster, and more intensely than previous generations. The old saying holds that it takes a village to raise a child.
title: Test #62: Creating an Ecosystem to Raise Our Adolescents

text: Colour blindness is a largely misunderstood genetic condition that affects millions of people worldwide, and a significant portion of those affected remain undiagnosed throughout their lives. According to various studies conducted in India, around 8% of men and 0.5% of women suffer from colour blindness, which means that almost 70 million Indians are potentially colour blind. The red-green type of this vision problem is the most common form, caused by a gene mutation located on the X-Chromosome. Colour blindness is a largely misunderstood genetic condition affecting millions of people, and a large number of those who have it remain undiagnosed for much of their lives. Men, having only 1-X Chromosome as opposed to the 2-X Chromosomes found in women, are far more susceptible to inheriting this condition from their parents. Studies estimate that colour blindness affects as many as 1 in 12 men globally, with the condition varying in degree from mild to severe across different individuals and populations. Despite being prevalent among Indians, knowledge and understanding of colour blindness in India remains extremely poor. Most of the general population holds the misconception that colour blindness means seeing the world only in shades of black and white. In reality, most people with colour blindness cannot discriminate between only certain colours, primarily red-green or blue-yellow combinations. The condition is congenital in the majority of cases, meaning it is present from birth, and as a result, many people may remain unaware of their condition for their entire lives. The disorder does not cause total blindness in any form and has absolutely no connection to a person’s level of intelligence. Colour blindness can interfere with daily life in ways that range from the serious to the seemingly minor. Common problems that individuals with this condition may encounter on a daily basis include misinterpreting traffic lights, facing a negative impact on academic performance, an inability to match clothes correctly, difficulties in working with colour-coded charts or maps, challenges with choosing ripe fruit, and problems with interpreting colour signals in various professional settings. Many of these difficulties can go entirely unnoticed until the person is formally diagnosed with the condition. Colour blindness can interfere with everyday life in ways that extend from the serious to the seemingly trivial, including misreading traffic signals, academic difficulties, and problems interpreting colour-coded information in professional environments. This makes early screening and diagnosis particularly important, especially for school-going children. It is important to note that colour blindness is not a single uniform condition but encompasses multiple distinct types. The red-green variety is the most common, while blue-yellow colour blindness and complete colour blindness, also known as achromatopsia, are considerably less common. Although colour blindness is most frequently genetic in origin, it can also develop as a result of other medical conditions such as diabetes mellitus, glaucoma, cataracts, retinal diseases, optic nerve disease, and brain injury. Additionally, ageing and the use of certain medicines have also been known to cause or worsen colour vision deficiency in affected individuals. Any change in colour vision should therefore be evaluated by an ophthalmologist without delay, as it may indicate an underlying serious eye or neurological condition. Testing of colour vision is considered necessary for children and adults who have diabetes or any chronic eye disease. Unfortunately, colour blindness awareness is not high enough in India to facilitate widespread testing in schools for every child. Although no permanent cure exists for genetically determined colour blindness, some individuals can benefit from the use of colour-filter glasses, which aid in discriminating between different colours. Schools, workplaces, and other environments rely heavily on colour codes, making it necessary to create colourblind-friendly surroundings wherever possible.
title: Test #63: Colour Blindness: A Hidden Vision Condition

text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has unsettled the field of Social Sciences in ways that were neither imagined nor predicted even as recently as 2018-2020. Within just 3 to 4 years of the widespread adoption of large language models, nearly 1,200 universities across more than 85 countries have had to revisit their academic integrity policies, according to reports compiled by global higher education bodies between 2022 and 2025. ChatGPT alone, launched in late 2022, crossed 100 million users within 60 days the fastest adoption of any consumer technology in recorded history. AI has brought a rapid reconfiguration in all 3-key components of higher education: reading, thinking, and writing. The single most consequential transformation that AI has brought to Liberal Arts education is not the ease of information access, though that is significant. It is, rather, the widening distrust between students and faculty. When a student submits a thoughtful, well-argued piece of writing, the first instinct of many teachers today is suspicion rather than appreciation. Although AI-detection tools are available and widely marketed, they have not remedied this growing atmosphere of mutual distrust. The impact on students who are genuinely motivated to write well can be deeply discouraging, even debilitating. AI has not merely made the work of certain teachers easier or harder it has displaced the very centrality of the teacher in the modern classroom. Students are increasingly sceptical about whether their faculty can offer something that ChatGPT cannot deliver faster and more conveniently. In many universities, the primary reason students attend classes at all is the enforcement of strict attendance policies rather than any intrinsic motivation to learn through discussion or debate. One can sense this scepticism in the questions students now raise openly: "What is the point of reading long articles when we can get good marks by reading the summary, which is just a prompt away?" This question, unsettling as it is, reflects a genuine and rational calculation on the part of students navigating an environment where effort and reward have been decoupled by technology. The consequences of this shift are visible in institutional responses across the world. Faced with the difficulty of assessing authentic student work, many universities are abandoning written assignments and returning to traditional examinations as the most reliable method of evaluation. The underlying logic is that, despite their well-documented limitations, in-person exams are more resistant to AI manipulation than take-home assignments. However, this reversal carries its own serious cost. Liberal Arts programmes have, for decades, championed written assignments as the primary vehicle for cultivating critical thinking, independent analysis, and intellectual self-expression. A retreat to examinations that emphasise memorisation and rote recall endangers the foundational goal of Liberal Arts education the development of a reflective, critical, and autonomous mind. There is also the question of originality. At one level, AI tools appear to function as a levelling device, making sophisticated language accessible to students who may not have grown up in English-medium environments, thereby democratising expression. Yet it is equally undeniable that the greatest casualty of the AI revolution within academia is writing as a distinct and disciplined genre. Within higher education, writing has long been valued not merely as a means of communication but as evidence of thought proof that a student has processed, questioned, and synthesised ideas on their own terms. In the current era of generalised, algorithmically produced content, what truly distinguishes one student's work from another's is originality. Students are increasingly sceptical about whether their faculty can offer something that ChatGPT cannot deliver faster and more conveniently, and the strict attendance policies that compel physical presence in classrooms do little to restore genuine intellectual engagement.
title: Test #64: Teaching Liberal Arts in the Era of ChatGPT

text: The eradication of polio stands among the greatest public health achievements of our time, and in India, it demonstrated what becomes possible when political will is matched by sustained institutional discipline. India was officially certified wild poliovirus-free on March 27, 2014 a milestone that many once considered impossible for a country of India’s size, complexity, and deeply uneven public health infrastructure. The journey to that certification had spanned decades, with the Global Polio Eradication Initiative gaining momentum globally from 1988 onwards, reducing worldwide cases by more than 99.99 percent over the following 3 decades. As of April 21, 2026, however, 3 cases of wild polio have been reported in Afghanistan and 1 case in Pakistan stark reminders that the path to a truly polio-free world remains fragile and unfinished, even as India marks more than 1200 days without a new reported case. The Global Polio Eradication Initiative, which has been operational since 1988-2026, has brought the world close to the finish line, but the final stretch has proven to be the most difficult. History is unambiguous on one critical point: diseases are careless of geographical and political boundaries, and no country’s gains are fully secure while the virus persists anywhere in the world. Polio-free certification is frequently interpreted as closure, when in fact the virus remains dangerously close to India’s borders. Polio-free status must therefore be actively maintained against a pathogen that can spread silently and cross undetected borders at any time. The greatest threat to any hard-won public health achievement is complacency the dangerous assumption that an extended absence of cases signals permanent victory. India has structured its surveillance systems precisely to counter that complacency. In addition to tracking acute flaccid paralysis cases across its healthcare network, India also conducts environmental surveillance by testing sewage samples across more than 50 strategic sites nationwide, intercepting the poliovirus before it can permanently impair a child’s mobility. India’s response protocol is explicit and unambiguous: even a single environmental positive result would trigger a coordinated, large-scale immunisation campaign, the kind of preparedness that is ingrained only within a truly mature public health system. True success, therefore, is measured not solely by the absence of disease, but by the strength of the systems that stand ready to prevent its return at any moment. The elimination of polio in India succeeded because 2,400,000 vaccinators and 150,000 supervisors were mobilised during National Immunisation Days, reaching communities that formal health infrastructure had consistently underserved for generations. Before the disruption caused by Covid-19, this sustained effort ran through National Immunisation Day and Sub-National Immunisation Days every year, maintaining an unbroken cadence of outreach. That sustained cadence was not incidental to the programme’s success it was the precise mechanism through which programme presence was gradually converted into population trust. The elimination of polio in India succeeded in part because such a large number of vaccinators and supervisors were deployed during National Immunisation Days, reaching communities that had long been underserved by formal healthcare systems. At that scale, logistics was only part of the challenge, and trust was the other and trust, unlike medicine, could not be mandated from above. The architecture behind this effort was deliberately multi-sectoral. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provided the policy direction and the essential resources. At the same time, Rotary International, UNICEF, the World Health Organization, and other partners of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative bridged the critical gap between government reach and genuine community acceptance. This distinction carries a direct strategic implication for any large-scale public health initiative anywhere in the world.
title: Test #65: Sustaining India’s Polio-Free Legacy

text: Land pooling mechanisms, particularly Town Planning (TP) schemes, have emerged as the most credible and widely tested alternative to compulsory acquisition. Under the TP scheme model, landowners voluntarily contribute approximately 25%-40% of their land to provide for essential infrastructure such as roads, parks, public amenities, and housing for economically weaker sections of society. The remaining land, constituting between 60%-75% of the original holding, is returned to landowners as reconstituted plots that are better shaped, properly serviced, and substantially more valuable than the original parcels. Urban infrastructure projects across India have historically depended upon the compulsory acquisition of land, a process that spans back well over 1000 years of statecraft in various forms across the subcontinent. Even before 2013, acquisition processes were time-consuming and frequently contested in courts and in communities across the country. Between 1976 and 2024, several States attempted to address this challenge through innovative land management mechanisms, and the gap between planned infrastructure and actual implementation widened steadily. Plans covering areas of 800-1200 hectares were routinely under-executed due to the persistent inability of authorities to mobilise land in a timely and cost-effective manner. Under the land pooling model, landowners voluntarily contribute a portion of their land for infrastructure development and receive back a share of the developed and serviced land in return. This method substantially reduces the need for compulsory acquisition and distributes the benefits of development equitably among all stakeholders. The TP scheme, widely implemented in the States of Gujarat and Maharashtra, stands among the most successful land-pooling models in the entire country. This process has become increasingly complex and financially burdensome since the enactment of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. The inclusion of rehabilitation and resettlement provisions after 2013 further increased the financial obligations of governments, making large-scale land acquisition for urban infrastructure projects increasingly unviable across dozens of cities with populations exceeding 1000-5000 persons per square kilometre. This integrated method combines land assembly, infrastructure provision, and cost recovery within a single administrative framework. A defining strength of the TP scheme is its participatory and people-centric approach, which gives landowners a direct stake in the outcome of the development process. The TP scheme is also financially self-sustaining. Incremental charges from landowners are recovered during the course of development rather than being demanded as large upfront payments. Compared with conventional land acquisitions, TP schemes significantly reduce displacement of residents and communities, ensure equitable sharing of development benefits, and enable faster urban development while also preserving environmentally sensitive areas. The TP scheme’s core strength lies in its participatory and people-centric approach, which ensures that landowners retain a direct and meaningful stake in the development process. Recognising this potential, the Government of India has actively promoted TP schemes since 2019 as a preferred mechanism for urban land management. Land pooling is not a new concept in India. In Gujarat, it was introduced nearly 100 years before the present day and was formally codified under the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976. Over time, more than 1,000 sq. km of land across the cities of Ahmedabad, Surat, Rajkot, Vadodara, and Gandhinagar have been planned and developed through TP schemes. Maharashtra, however, failed to update its statutory provisions for enabling TP schemes consistently, though Pune and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority have recently adopted the model to provide serviced land in peripheral areas. In Rajasthan, land pooling provisions had been recognised in statute since 2016, but implementation was limited by a lack of institutional experience. Modifications have since been introduced to land-value calculations to ensure that the financial burden.
title: Test #66: Land Pooling: A Path to Urban Development

text: The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow corridor just 33 km wide at its most constricted point, connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and ultimately to the Arabian Sea. It is the world’s single most critical oil transit chokepoint, through which, during 2023-2025, approximately 20% of the world’s liquefied natural gas and 25% of all seaborne oil passed every year. In 2025 alone, 20 million barrels of oil and oil products moved through this route every single day, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Around 3,000 ships sailed through the strait each month before the outbreak of the war in early 2026, and there are 8 major islands within the strait, 7 of which are controlled by Iran. Iran’s physical command over the strait is not merely political it is deeply geographical. The weaponisation of the strait is not without historical precedent. During the 1980s, across the eight years of the Iran-Iraq war, both sides systematically targeted fuel tankers moving through Persian Gulf waters, turning a commercial waterway into a theatre of asymmetric conflict. In more recent years, Iran repeatedly warned the international community that it would close the strait if it came under military attack. When the United States and Israel launched a war on February 28, 2026, beginning with the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Tehran responded exactly as it had promised. It retaliated against Israel and Arab nations in the Gulf, and it took effective control of the Strait of Hormuz. The number of ships passing through the strait daily, which had exceeded 100 before the war, fell by over 90% almost immediately, sending shockwaves through global energy markets, insurance sectors, and the economies of energy-import-dependent nations. India, one of the world’s largest importers of Gulf oil, was among the countries hit hardest by the resulting fuel price surge and supply uncertainty. The strait’s strategic significance grew steadily after oil was discovered across the Persian Gulf region in the early 20th century. The post-War oil boom transformed the region fundamentally and irreversibly. All Persian Gulf nations Iran, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait have depended on the strait for access to the Arabian Sea and to global markets. While Iran, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Oman possess ports outside Gulf waters, several smaller nations are entirely dependent on Hormuz for both exports and essential imports including food, medicine, and technology products. Hormuz is also a key corridor for fertiliser exports from the Gulf region, making its disruption a matter not only of energy security but of food security for many import-dependent nations across Asia and Africa. During the 40 days of intensive bombing, the United States and Israel inflicted substantial material damage on Iran’s aerial and naval infrastructure. Yet these strikes proved insufficient to compel Iran to reopen the strait. Iran deployed cheap, asymmetric, and disruptive weapons to impose disproportionate costs on vessels that attempted to pass without permission from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Several ships that tried to navigate the strait without IRGC clearance came under direct attack. Fuel prices climbed sharply. Insurance and shipping costs soared to levels not seen in decades. When U.S. President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire with Iran on April 8, 2026, he declared that Iran had agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The truce came into effect, but both sides held fundamentally different interpretations of its terms. Iran demanded a simultaneous ceasefire in Lebanon, while Israel intensified its bombing campaign there instead. When Iran refused to reopen the strait under these conditions, Mr. Trump announced a blockade of Iranian ports on April 12, barring Iranian vessels from passing through American-controlled waters in the Gulf of Oman. Iran’s response was to cancel direct negotiations with the United States and to formally establish a new regulatory body the Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA).
title: Test #67: Hormuz: The Strait Where America Stalled

text: The Agrometeorologist, says that rising temperatures and erratic rainfall now expose fruit crops to multiple simultaneous stresses. Every summer, the orchards of Muzaffarpur in Bihar fill with a heavy, sweet scent the unmistakable promise of ripening litchi. The Shahi litchi, prized for its succulent white flesh and delicate flavour, is a GI-tagged variety that has defined the identity of this region for well over 1,000 years. In 2024-25, the litchi crop had already shown signs of stress, but the season of 2025-26 proved far more devastating. Scientists estimate that nearly 70% of Bihar’s litchi crop has been wiped out this year, a staggering loss running into hundreds of crores of rupees. Vegetables and Flowers Growers Association, estimated that the state’s apple economy could shrink from Rs 5,000-6,000 crore to just Rs 1,500-2,000 crore this season. Temperatures breached 38-DegreeC during April and May, causing massive, premature fruit drop. The same erratic weather dry westerly winds that blackened the skin, dried up the pulp, and cracked the fruit was then followed by unseasonal rain and hailstorms that created conditions perfect for an aggressive outbreak of the litchi stink bug. This almost dystopian scene, described by helpless farmers, has been caused by the combination of unseasonal rain in the last two months and the destructive attack of the stink bug pest, a problem that local scientists say has grown beyond anything ever recorded. Last year, farmer was able to use earnings from the harvest to pay for his daughter’s school fees and wedding expenses for another daughter. This year, he has nothing. The damage is only compounded by the fact that horticulture farming is capital-intensive and a far riskier endeavour than typical cropping, leaving farmers with little cushion when things go wrong. Summer once meant certainty in the orchards of Maharashtra. Mango trees in Konkan would bend under the weight of the Alphonso fruit, banana growers in Jalgaon would ready truckloads for markets across north India, and vineyards in Nashik would race against time to meet export deadlines. This year, many farmers say the season has instilled fear and unease. Agriculture department studies showed widespread losses in north Maharashtra, especially in Nashik and Dhule districts, while mango growers in Konkan reported one of the weakest harvests in recent years. In the Konkan belt, Alphonso farmers say flowering patterns have become erratic due to warmer winters, while unseasonal rain and humidity trigger fungal attacks and fruit drop. Nearly half the bunches cracked or developed fungus after rain. Export agents rejected the crop, saying it was not fit for Europe. "One unseasonal spell of rain is enough to destroy an entire year of work," he said. Himachal Pradesh looks headed for one of its worst apple seasons in memory, with farmers reporting losses of up to 70% due to prolonged erratic weather. Traditional varieties such as Royal Delicious and Red Delicious are among the worst hit, with damage reaching 80% in some areas. Apple orchards did not receive the requisite chilling hours due to delayed and comparatively less snowfall, affecting bud development and the fruitsetting cycle. Scientists and agriculture experts agree that adaptation not short-term compensation will determine whether fruit farming in India remains viable. ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture director T. Damodaran says that India’s litchi production is expected to go down by 40% because of crop loss in Bihar alone. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has, in the last decade, released 2,177 crop varieties targeting various climate vulnerabilities. India is now developing climate-resilient varieties HRMN-99, Anna, and Golden Dorset for apples, and Arka Udaya and Arka Suprabhath as varieties of mango that can cope with unpredictable weather and boost farm productivity. Studies have shown how techniques like cluster spraying and lowering canopy size have been effective in combating the stink bug on litchi fruit.
title: Test #68: Fruits are Felling Prey to Changing Weather

text: On May 22, 2026, the Pentagon released a second batch of declassified photos and videos showing what appear to be unexplained flying objects. But to assess the plausibility of alien visitors, it’s necessary to understand the obstacles that an extraterrestrial vessel would need to overcome to reach Earth. No object can reach or exceed light speed (roughly 3,00,000 km per second). But well before that threshold, engineering constraints begin to assert themselves. Limited fuel and potential for structural damage will restrict a craft’s speed. There is no universally accepted upper limit on interstellar flight speeds, but studies tend to converge around 30,000 km/s 10% of the speed of light as a realistic cruise velocity. At this speed, a journey of 10 light years will take roughly 100 years. There is no evidence of alien life in our solar system. So, visitors would likely have to come from another star system in the Milky Way. Proxima Centauri, the star closest to our Sun, is about 4.25 lightyears away. Since only a fraction of stars are thought to host intelligent life, the nearest alien civilization if one exists is surely much farther away than Proxima. Interstellar space offers some advantages. Lack of atmosphere means there is no drag. So, when the ship reaches its cruise speed, it can shut its propulsion system and coast to the final destination. But lack of atmosphere also means there is nothing to slow the ship down. Ideally, the propulsion system would have to both accelerate and decelerate. One propulsion strategy employs a high-powered laser to push a ship through space. The beam is projected from a stationary array near the home planet and directed toward a thin reflective sail attached to the ship. The beam’s photons exert radiation pressure on the sail, propelling the ship forward. This approach requires no onboard fuel. But the energy needed to operate the laser would be staggering. Beamed propulsion also provides no mechanism for deceleration. At best, this method could be deployed as part of a hybrid strategy that uses a separate system for deceleration. A more practical solution is rocket propulsion. Rockets generate thrust by expelling high-velocity exhaust. By reversing the direction of the exhaust, rockets can also be used to slow the ship down. But their main disadvantage is that rockets must carry their own fuel in addition to passengers, habitat and lifesustaining systems. In other words, you need fuel to transport your fuel. All human missions have used chemical rocket propulsion, but a craft travelling at 30,000 km/s would need more fuel than all the mass in the observable universe. Antimatter propulsion is theoretically the most efficient option. When antimatter comes into contact with ordinary matter, the two undergo mutual annihilation and 100% of their combined mass is converted into energy. This makes it possible to achieve the same cruise velocity one-tenth the speed of light with fuel accounting for less than a quarter of the ship’s total mass. The downside is that antimatter is extremely unstable and difficult to make. To date, particle physicists have produced less than 20 billionths of a gram of antimatter. Moreover, these particles had lifespans lasting only fractions of a second and a price tag in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Nuclear fusion offers a more viable alternative. Fusion engines remain aspirational, but they could, in theory, produce 10 million times more energy per kilogram than chemical rockets. Still, a fusion-powered ship with a cruise velocity of 30,000 km/s would need fuel equivalent to 150 times the mass of the ship itself. We now come to ship design. Interstellar space has a sparse smattering of microscopic cosmic dust. At 30,000 km/s, the tiny grains would hit the hull with the energy of a .22-calibre bullet. Surviving the onslaught would require no less than a fortress with complex shielding, increasing the total mass of the ship and driving up fuel use. No single law of physics prohibits an interstellar voyage to Earth.
title: Test #69: Could Aliens Reach Earth? - Physics Say No

text: The year 2026 marks 15 years since Godrej officially closed its last typewriter production unit in India. These machines now live on merely as vintage curios in antique shops and collectors’ shelves. It is genuinely hard to believe that these devices were once regarded as nothing short of magical. Typewriters arrived in India in the early 1900s, usually imported from Britain or the United States, and as a result they were extraordinarily expensive. Even as late as the 1930s, a brand-new Remington typewriter cost many times as much as a bicycle placing it firmly out of reach for most ordinary households. In his book Everyday Technology: Machines and the Making of India’s Modernity, published in 2013, British historian David Arnold notes that there were barely 1,000 of these devices in the entire country in 1901-1902. Before typewriters arrived, everything had to be handwritten, and many genuinely feared the machine would signal the death of calligraphy and they were not entirely wrong. From those slender beginnings of barely 1,000 machines at the turn of the century, the typewriter rapidly became a mainstay of offices across India. India between 1955-1965 and well beyond, as women claimed their right to economic independence through the simple but powerful act of typing. Typing and secretarial schools mushroomed in every major city. Newspapers began to carry advertisements seeking people who could competently operate these machines, and a new kind of professional identity was born almost overnight. By the time of Indian Independence in 1947, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru was keen that India manufacture its own machines domestically. Buoyed by government support, Godrej released its first commercial typewriter model in 1955, marking a defining moment in the country’s industrial and cultural history. Typing schools swelled with enrollments as the device transformed from a luxury import into an accessible tool of modern Indian office life. The typewriter did something far more significant than merely accelerate the pace of office correspondence. It helped create, in India and across the rest of the world, what historian Arnold describes as "the image of the stylish, independent and technologically savvy modern girl." Unlike other widely accepted professions available to women at the time such as teaching or nursing secretarial and typing work offered a new kind of accessibility, and large numbers of women took to it with enthusiasm and purpose. The typewriter became, in a very real sense, an instrument of social emancipation, opening the doors of professional life to women who had previously found those doors firmly shut. Indian cinema, alert as always to shifting social realities, was quick to reflect this transformation. The device appeared prominently in films as a sign of the changing times. The glamorous typist in Hindi films was simultaneously a cultural trope and a social statement sometimes cast as "the other woman" in the hero’s life, but more meaningfully portrayed as an ordinary working woman with her own dreams, struggles, and ambitions. These cinematic heroines, hard at work on machines that signified modernity and freedom, blazed a trail that countless real women followed. The typewriter, humble and mechanical as it was, became a gateway to professional identity, financial independence, and a quietly radical reimagining of what women could be and do. From fewer than 1,000 machines in 1901-1902 to an entire national industry by 1955, and from anonymous office tool to a powerful symbol of women’s liberation few inventions have carried such unexpected social weight in the story of modern India. In Mr and Mrs ‘55, released in 1955, a bubbly young woman named Julie works confidently in a newspaper office, representing the new generation of capable urban women. In Paigham, released in 1959, Vyjayanthimala plays Manju, a young woman who has just completed her Bachelor’s degree. When a friend asks what she intends to do next, she replies without hesitation that she wants a job which is precisely why she has completed a course in shorthand and typing.
title: Test #70: Typewriter, Typing, Women and Changed Work

text: The 1986 FIFA World Cup, held across Mexico over a month-long tournament, marked a significant turning point in how Indian audiences experienced international football. Doordarshan, India’s state broadcaster began live telecasts of select matches during those June days, symbolically setting in motion a culture of watching football and international sport on Indian television screens. The broadcast coincided with the second day of the tournament, with Mexico hosting the world’s 1986 competition, and different accounts place different matches as the first to have been carried live. The 1986 World Cup, staged across Mexico during an entire month of competitive football, represented a defining moment in the way Indian viewers first encountered the sport in real time. The defending champions, who had systematically dismantled Brazil’s celebrated 1982 style of play, appeared in their distinctive blue jerseys against a compact Argentine side that looked to its central figure for virtually every meaningful contribution on the pitch. That figure was Diego Maradona. Maradona scored the first of his five goals at the 1986 World Cup in the match against Italy, a strike of quiet deception and technical precision that the watching world scarcely registered in the moment. Bangladesh, whose expatriate population had already demonstrated an organic and long-standing connection with the sport, began its own live telecast with considerably less institutional friction, while India debated the matter in Parliament before broadcasts could begin. Brazil opened their campaign with a 1-0 victory over Spain, a match that generated its own controversies. Spanish attackers were denied a legitimate goal when the ball crossed Carlos’s goal line and returned to play without the referee awarding it. Brazil’s decisive goal, scored by Socrates, came from a position adjudged offside, making the result contentious by any fair measure. Italy faced Argentina in what would become one of the more enduring early-round matches of Mexico 1986. The goal arrived without announcement, understated among a series of increasingly spectacular contributions that would follow over the course of the tournament. In that same summer of 1986, India’s collective sporting psyche had already been shaken weeks earlier, when Javed Miandad struck a six off the final ball at Sharjah in April to deny India victory in the Austral-Asia Cup final. The psychological weight of that moment shaped Indian sporting consciousness for nearly two decades, from 1986 to the mid-2000s. Against this backdrop, the question of whether Indian audiences would be granted access to World Cup telecasts at all carried genuine weight. The long-running dispute over India’s broadcast rights for the 2026 World Cup produced an echo of those earlier anxieties, drawing a direct line between the institutional battles of 1986 and the commercial disputes of the present day. When sports telecast rights become primarily a matter of revenue calculation, with interest determined by match scheduling and advertising potential, the relationship between broadcaster and audience shifts fundamentally. Sports watching in societies with developed sporting cultures carry the character of a civic obligation, and the denial of broadcast access produces public outrage. In India, the response has historically been more muted. Prasar Bharti, India’s public broadcaster, communicated to the courts that no moral obligation existed to ensure Indian football fans received access to the tournament. The contrast with 1994 is instructive. When Roberto Baggio struck his penalty over the crossbar in the final at the Rose Bowl in Los Angeles, Indian audiences watched through the night, television sets illuminating households as dawn approached, sleep surrendered willingly in the service of the game. In that year, the absence of convenient broadcast hours produced no institutional conflict, and Indian audiences simply watched, across whatever hours the time difference imposed.
title: Test #71: Sports Watcher to Sports Consumer - World Cup

text: The Mahabharat remains one of humanity’s most profound and enduring reflections on the spiritual consequences of large-scale war. The great battle of Kurukshetra was not merely a political struggle between two rival groups of princes but a catastrophic confrontation between dharm and adharm, between righteousness and moral disorder. Spiritual traditions have long viewed humanity as active participants in a shared field of consciousness, a view documented across more than 3000 years of philosophical and religious writing from at least 1200 BCE onward. When violence erupts on a massive scale, that collective field is severely disturbed, affecting not just individuals but entire civilisations across generations. Ancient Indian thought, which produced texts spanning roughly 800-1200 years between 500 BCE and 700 CE, described this disruption as adharm, a fundamental disturbance in the moral and cosmic balance of existence. Violent acts affect not only societies and nations but also the subtle psychological fabric of civilisation itself, leaving behind layers of suffering that often persist for 1000 years or more after the original conflict has ended. Records from periods as wide-ranging as 1350-1947 CE show that no major civilisation has escaped the long shadow of collective trauma. When violence erupts on a catastrophic scale, that shared collective field is deeply disturbed, shaping not just individuals but entire societies across time. Modern psychology has identified and described this phenomenon as collective trauma. Societies frequently carry deep emotional scars that survive for many generations after a violent event. Fear, instability, moral confusion, and unresolved hatred continue to shape cultures long after the battlefield has fallen completely silent. Trauma spreads outward through communities like ripples across the surface of still water, influencing future conflicts and leaving behind psychological debris that may require centuries to fully address. Millions of warriors perished on the battlefield, families and entire lineages disappeared from the face of the earth, and the established social order collapsed under the weight of unimaginable destruction. Yet even the victors who survived found no lasting joy in their triumph. Yudhishthir, who was crowned king of Hastinapur following the war, was overwhelmed by grief and an acute sense of guilt. The apparent triumph of righteousness over injustice could not erase the profound suffering caused by the destruction of teachers, dear friends, and close relatives. Victory felt deeply hollow because it had been purchased at an enormous cost to human life and familial bonds. Yudhishthir, crowned the ruler of Hastinapur after the Great War, was overcome by grief and a deep sense of personal guilt. The Mahabharat repeatedly reminds its readers that war leaves behind wounds far deeper than any physical destruction, wounds that reside in the conscience of the survivors and in the memory of the civilisation itself. Among the most symbolically significant aspects of the Mahabharat’s aftermath is Krishn’s deliberate withdrawal to Dwarka following the conclusion of the war. Although he had guided the Pandavs at every critical moment and had delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjun on the battlefield, Krishn moved away from Kurukshetra once the fighting was over. Dwarka represented a place of distance from the psychic residue of violence and a space where civilisation could gradually rebuild itself. Ancient traditions held a firm belief that land absorbs human emotions and actions over time. Sacred places are created slowly through sustained meditation, prayer, and righteous conduct, while battlefields become permanently saturated with suffering, death, and despair. The Mahabharat, however, does not completely reject war as an option. Krishn made repeated attempts at diplomacy and negotiated compromise before the conflict began in earnest. Even the concession of five villages to the Pandavs could have prevented the entire catastrophe.
title: Test #72: No Joy in Aftermath of War

text: The Thakali people of Nepal number only around 15,000 globally, yet their culinary tradition is considered one of the richest and most distinctive in the entire Himalayan region. Thakalis hail from Thak-sat-se, also known as the Thak Khola region, located in the Kali Gandaki River valley of the Mustang District in north-central Nepal. Their history as a community is inseparable from the ancient salt trade routes that once connected the high Himalayas to the plains below, and their cuisine reflects centuries of cultural exchange along those very routes. The Nepal-Tibet War of 1855-1856 proved to be a turning point for the community, rewarding their role as soldiers and translators with far-reaching business privileges. The culinary exchanges that took place along these ancient trade routes were instrumental in shaping what Thakali food is today. Himalayan staples such as buckwheat, millets, and timur the distinctively aromatic Nepali or Sichuan pepper were combined with Tibetan techniques and, through the salt routes, with Indian spices including turmeric, cumin, ginger, and fenugreek. Unique to Thakali cooking are ingredients like jimbu, a dried herb from the onion and garlic family, sukuti or dried meat, gundruk which is fermented leafy greens, and sinki, made from fermented radish roots. These are not merely flavouring agents but define the entire character of the cuisine its earthiness, its depth, and its slow, deliberate approach to heat and seasoning. A traditional Thakali meal is a carefully assembled experience. It typically begins with kanchemba, crispy buckwheat fries, and jimbu-tempered potatoes. At its heart sits daal-bhaat lentils and rice alongside tarkari or vegetables, achaar or pickles, gundruk, sekuwa which is grilled meat, and masu, a meat curry. Dhido, a thick porridge made from buckwheat or millet, and ghoken, which are buckwheat pancakes mixed with homemade aromatic ghee, are equally integral components. Most dishes are slow-cooked, lightly tempered, and layered with flavour rather than overwhelmed by spice. The 1927 abolition of the salt trade monopoly forced Thakalis to migrate from Mustang and take up agriculture, animal husbandry, and the hotel business a second confusion trap that revisits the pivotal historical moment which redirected the community’s energy into the very culinary tradition being celebrated today. Under then Prime Minister Jung Bahadur Rana, the Thakali community was granted multiple business opportunities including salt trade, mining, import-export of animals and food items, spices, and customs collection. Danish scholar Michael Vinding, in his 1998 book The Thakali: A Himalayan Ethnography, documents how this period of prosperity fundamentally reshaped the community’s economic identity. However, the tide turned in 1927, when the government abolished the old customs-collecting system and ended the community’s monopoly on the salt trade. Faced with the loss of their traditional economic base, Thakalis adapted with remarkable resilience migrating southward from Mustang, taking up agriculture and animal husbandry, and establishing hotels and restaurants across Nepal’s growing towns and cities. This instinct for adaptation, forged over generations of high-altitude trade and travel, would eventually bring Thakali cuisine to a far wider audience than the remote valleys of Mustang had ever imagined. Now, this tradition is making its way into India. Vivek Man Sherchan, a Kathmandu-based engineer-turned-entrepreneur and himself a Thakali, operates Jimbu Thakali, a restaurant chain he founded in 2016 that has since grown to four outlets three in Kathmandu and one in Patan. He is preparing to open the chain’s first Indian outlet at M3M IFC, Sector 66, Gurugram, in Delhi-NCR. His plan to enter the Indian market in 2021 was disrupted by the pandemic, but the vision remained intact. "Delhi-NCR might have many places serving Nepali food, but we wanted to bring authentic Thakali flavours which go beyond the stereotypes," Vivek has said.
title: Test #73: From the Salt Routes of Mustang - Thakali Cuisine

text: In a 163-page judgment delivered on May 22, 2026, Justice Mini Pushkarna of the Delhi High Court examined one of the most consequential questions in modern digital commerce: can a company legally purchase a rival’s registered trademark as a keyword on Google Ads so that its advertisements appear first when consumers search for that trademark? The case, initiated in early 2013 by Hindware Limited a well-established sanitaryware brand against Google India, Google LLC, Grohe India Private Limited, and Cera Sanitaryware Limited, had been building through the courts for over 13 years before this ruling. The Trade Marks Act, specifically Section 29(6), forms the core legal provision at the centre of this dispute, and Google’s AdWords programme which has been permitted to use trademarks as keywords in India since 2009 sits at the heart of the controversy. The facts of the case are straightforward. Understanding how Google’s keyword advertising system operates is essential to grasping why this case matters. Google’s AdWords programme allows advertisers to bid for specific words or phrases called ‘keywords’ which trigger a sponsored advertisement when a user enters those terms into Google Search. When multiple advertisers compete for the same keyword, including a trademarked term, Google conducts an auction and earns a Cost-Per-Click amount as revenue from the winning bidder. The practical consequence is that a consumer specifically searching for Brand A may find Brand B displayed prominently at the top of their results effectively redirecting consumer intent toward a competitor. Hindware contended that this constitutes use of its trademark "in advertising" within the meaning of Section 29(6) of the Trade Marks Act, and that consumers searching specifically for ‘Hindware’ were plainly seeking Hindware’s products, making the diversion to a rival’s site an act of both infringement and unfair competition. Google’s defence rested on the technical distinction between visible and invisible use. The company argued that keywords function as backend triggers invisible to the user at the moment of searching and that such use therefore cannot constitute ‘use’ of a trademark within the legal meaning of the Trade Marks Act. Google further argued that sponsored search results are clearly labelled with the prefix ‘Ad’, sufficiently distinguishing them from organic results and thereby eliminating the likelihood of confusion. The company also maintained that permitting competitors to bid on established brand names as keywords serves a pro-competitive purpose, enabling smaller firms to compete against larger, more visible incumbents. Until 2009, Google had not permitted the use of trademarks as keywords in India a policy it maintained in line with its approach in European Union and European Free Trade Association countries but changed this practice after 2009, creating the conditions that gave rise to this very dispute. The Delhi High Court rejected Google’s arguments in full. In early 2013, Hindware discovered that its competitors Grohe India and Cera Sanitaryware had purchased the trademark ‘Hindware’ as a keyword through Google’s AdWords programme. As a direct result, whenever a consumer typed ‘Hindware’ into the Google search engine, the first result displayed was the website of Cera. Similarly, searches for ‘Hindware Sanitary’ or ‘Hindware Sanitaryware’ returned Grohe’s website as the topmost result. Hindware argued that its registered and well-known trademark, representing substantial goodwill built over decades, was being offered and auctioned by Google to its direct competitors without Hindware’s prior consent or approval. Cera and Grohe eventually settled with Hindware, leaving Google India and Google LLC as the remaining defendants in what became a defining test of how trademark law applies to digital advertising in India. It is the first comprehensive Indian judicial ruling to address the question of whether the backend, invisible use of a registered trademark as an advertising keyword constitutes infringement.
title: Test #74: DHC Landmark Ruling on Google Keyword Ads

text: We are witnessing a summer of soaring distrust, despair and discontent. Yet through this dark cloud, we see hope in how some students have held an ethical mirror to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). Earlier this month, 23 lakh students who had appeared for the medical entrance test (NEET) were devastated to learn that it was compromised and cancelled. While investigations were still underway to unearth the organised network for the paper ‘loot’, another trauma lay in store for those who took the class 12 CBSE exam. This year, CBSE introduced an on-screen marking (OSM) system for the class 12 exam. Answer sheets of 18 lakh students (amounting to over 90 lakhs for all subjects) were scanned, and the digitised copies sent for evaluation by teachers. Students have demanded re-evaluation of more than 11 lakh answer sheets. But the portal is now closed, and there could be many more who have been wronged. With only 30,000 schools, CBSE is much smaller than some state boards, such as Maharashtra, MP or Odisha, making the lapses all the more difficult to understand. What is even more shocking is the campaign where videos have been made by school principals and children, giving false statements about the OSM checking process being more efficient and less biased because marks are strictly on the basis of what is written in the answer sheet. A social media post by a student exclaims, “My school has gone MADDD”, lamenting that teachers were traumatising them to tell lies even though they had passed out of school last year, before the OSM. Indeed, such false propaganda to push for digital evaluation is deeply worrying. Digital marking is not the panacea that CBSE and the technology industry. claim it to be. Teachers who assessed the answer sheets this year have experienced an unsettling environment where they were regimented to work on screens, through often blurry scans, as they tried to decipher different handwriting, discern what students had written and make judgments about their answers. They were also being ‘watched’, as one teacher said, and the centre got a call if someone seemed to take longer. Their voices are being heard, albeit anonymously. Assessment is not a mechanical scrolling of our eyes on a page; it involves human cognitive processing with professional understanding. As teachers, we evaluate a student’s work with moral responsibility, we flip back and forth to decide what they understand and how to mark that fairly. Already, the multiple-choice question (MCQ) format of most of our entrance tests, chosen for being machine-scorable, is acutely limiting the value of what we assess. Tick marks on a page do not assess a student’s analytical understanding and ability to express ideas. More competitive examinations based on superficial MCQ or short-answer formats need speed and memory recall, pushing them into the commercial arms of the coaching industry. If we constrain teachers’ human acumen to assess by resorting to digital convenience, we will not be doing justice to our students. We risk cursorily eliminating them from the educational opportunities they deserve. We need to reframe school-leaving board examinations with assessment items and tasks that demand critical thinking, honed through better schooling. Technologies require responsible, knowledgeable and trustworthy decisions to nurture ingenuity with equity. Let our academic bodies win their trust and seriously reckon with those digital allurements that do not bode well for the future of our children. The students have admirably shown they are ready to work with us in this direction. Students who managed to overcome the malfunctioning portal saw staggering discrepancies in their marks and answer sheets. With no official help forthcoming, they posted on social media to warn others about the wrongly evaluated, badly scanned or mismatched sheets not even belonging to them. For this, some were trolled with perverse, abusive comments. Their anguished voices have mobilised the media towards sustained attention and sound investigative reports.
title: Test #75: CBSE's New Digital Marking System Failing Test

text: गणेश चतुर्थी का धार्मिक महत्व भाद्रपद शुक्ल पक्ष की चतुर्थी को गणेश चतुर्थी मनाई जाती है। धार्मिक मान्यता के अनुसार इसी तिथि को भगवान गणेश का प्राकट्य हुआ था। श्रद्धालु इस दिन विधि-विधान से गणपति की स्थापना कर दूर्वा, मोदक, लड्डू और पुष्प अर्पित करते हैं। वर्ष 2026 में गणेश चतुर्थी 14 सितंबर को और अनंत चतुर्दशी 25 सितंबर को होगी। 1893 में पुणे में तिलक ने गणेशोत्सव को सार्वजनिक रूप देने का प्रयास किया। उनका उद्देश्य धार्मिक आयोजन को सामाजिक एकता, जनजागरण और राष्ट्रीय चेतना के मंच के रूप में विकसित करना था। ब्रिटिश शासन के दौर में बड़े राजनीतिक जमावड़ों पर कई तरह की पाबंदियां थीं। ऐसे समय में धार्मिक-सांस्कृतिक आयोजन समाज के विभिन्न वर्गों को एक साथ लाने का माध्यम बने। गणेशोत्सव अब केवल धार्मिक अनुष्ठान तक सीमित नहीं है। यह कला, लोकसंस्कृति, सामुदायिक सहभागिता और सामाजिक चेतना से जुड़ा व्यापक पर्व बन चुका है। महाराष्ट्र में सार्वजनिक गणेशोत्सव ने सामाजिक एकता और स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन के दौर में जनजागरण का माध्यम बनने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। समय के साथ यह पर्व देश के विभिन्न हिस्सों और विदेशों में बसे भारतीय समुदायों तक पहुंच गया। बुद्धि और मंगल के प्रतीकसनातन परंपरा में भगवान गणेश को विघ्नहर्ता और बुद्धि-विवेक का अधिष्ठाता माना जाता है। धार्मिक विश्वास है कि किसी भी शुभ कार्य से पहले गणेश पूजन करने से कार्य निर्विघ्न संपन्न होता है। गणेश शब्द की व्याख्या गणों के ईश के रूप में की जाती है। वे भगवान शिव और माता पार्वती के पुत्र तथा शिवगणों के अधिपति माने जाते हैं। धार्मिक परंपराओं में गणेश को विद्या, बुद्धि, सिद्धि, समृद्धि और आनंद से भी जोड़ा गया है। बुधवार को भी गणेश आराधना का विशेष महत्व माना जाता है। धार्मिक और ज्योतिषीय मान्यताओं में बुध ग्रह को बुद्धि, वाणी, गणना और व्यापार से जोड़ा जाता है। हालांकि इससे जुड़े फल धार्मिक और ज्योतिषीय विश्वासों का हिस्सा हैं। गणेश के स्वरूप में छिपे जीवन-संदेश भगवान गणेश का स्वरूप प्रतीकों से समृद्ध माना जाता है। उनका विशाल मस्तक व्यापक चिंतन, छोटी आंखें एकाग्रता और बड़े कान अधिक सुनने की क्षमता का प्रतीक माने जाते हैं। उनकी सूंड सक्रियता और परिस्थितियों के अनुरूप स्वयं को ढालने की क्षमता का संकेत देती है। विशाल उदर को जीवन में मिलने वाली अच्छी-बुरी परिस्थितियों को धैर्यपूर्वक स्वीकार करने और उन्हें पचाने की क्षमता से जोड़ा जाता है। इसी कारण उन्हें ‘लंबोदर’ कहा जाता है। उनका एक टूटा हुआ दांत उन्हें ‘एकदंत’ नाम देता है। धार्मिक व्याख्याओं में इसे त्याग, ज्ञान और उद्देश्य के प्रति समर्पण का प्रतीक माना गया है। गणेश का वाहन मूषक भी अपने भीतर प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ समेटे है। धार्मिक व्याख्या में मूषक को चंचल मन, इच्छाओं और भटकती प्रवृत्तियों से जोड़ा जाता है। विशाल गणेश के साथ छोटे मूषक की कल्पना इस संदेश को व्यक्त करती है कि बुद्धि और विवेक से मन की चंचलता पर नियंत्रण पाया जा सकता है। चार भुजाओं में जीवन-दर्शन भगवान गणेश के चार हाथों में विभिन्न वस्तुओं का चित्रण मिलता है। इनमें पाश, अंकुश, मोदक और वरद अथवा अभय मुद्रा प्रमुख हैं। धार्मिक व्याख्याओं में पाश को आसक्ति पर नियंत्रण, अंकुश को मन को सही दिशा देने, मोदक को ज्ञान से मिलने वाले आनंद और वरदहस्त को कृपा एवं संरक्षण का प्रतीक माना जाता है। गणेश का संबंध महाभारत की रचना की प्रसिद्ध कथा से भी जुड़ा है। धार्मिक परंपरा के अनुसार महर्षि वेदव्यास ने महाभारत की रचना की और भगवान गणेश ने उसे लिपिबद्ध किया। कथा के अनुसार गणेश ने लगातार लिखने की शर्त रखी, जबकि व्यास ने प्रत्येक श्लोक का अर्थ समझने के बाद ही उसे लिखने की शर्त रखी। इस कथा ने गणेश को लेखन, ज्ञान और बुद्धि के प्रतीक के रूप में प्रतिष्ठित किया।
title: Test #01: Ganeshotsav - Budhi, Vivek Aur Mangal Ka Sandesh

text: मेरे मन में हमेशा यह सवाल आता रहा है कि आखिर इंसान यानी मानव जाति ने पत्र लिखना कब सीखा होगा या आदिमानव ने पहला पत्र कब और कैसे लिखा होगा। इन सभी सवालों का कोई भी प्रामाणिक जवाब शायद इतिहास की किताबों में दर्ज न हो। लेकिन अंदाजे से इतना तो कहा ही जा सकता है कि शायद जब मानव ने लिखना सीखा, तभी से उसने पत्र लिखना भी शुरू कर दिया होगा। भाषा वैज्ञानिकों के मतानुसार अपने मन की बात दूसरों तक पहुंचाने के लिए मानव ने सर्वप्रथम जिस लिपि का उपयोग किया, वह चित्र लिपि थी। यही कंदरावासी आदिमानव की आदि लिपि थी, या यूं कहें तो यही थी। इस लिपि ने केवल चित्रकला को ही पैदा नहीं किया, अपितु यही लेखन के इतिहास का भी प्राचीनतम प्रमाण बनी। इतना ही नहीं, चित्र लिपि के जरिए ही सूत्र लिपि और भाव मूलक लिपि का भी विकास हुआ। ये सभी चित्र लिपि के ही विकसित रूप हैं। चित्र व भाव मूलक लिपि में लिखे गए पत्रों का प्रमाण इतिहास में मिलता है, लेकिन वे बहुत अधिक प्राचीन प्रतीत नहीं होते हैं। इससे एक बात का अनुमान तो साफ तौर पर लगाया जा सकता है कि लेखन के इतिहास के साथ ही पत्र लेखन भी प्रारंभ हो गया होगा। लिपि का संबंध भाव संप्रेषण से है। इतने लंबे समय से प्रयोग में आते-आते पत्र लेखन आज एक उपयोगी कला का रूप धारण कर चुका है। पत्र आज के जीवन का एक अनिवार्य अंग बन चुका है। एक प्रकार से देखा जाए तो मानव के दैनिक जीवन में पत्र के उपयोग के बिना काम नहीं चल सकता। दूर-दूर रहने वाले परिजनों व मित्रों से ही केवल हम पत्र के जरिए बात नहीं करते, अपितु प्रशासनिक कामों के लिए भी हम अधिकतर पत्र का ही उपयोग करते हैं। सारा सरकारी काम-काज तो लगभग पत्राचार से ही चलता है। अगर पत्र लेखन को उपयोगी कला के साथ ललित कला भी कहा जाए तो बिलकुल गलत नहीं होगा। आज पत्र लेखन विधा की अपनी एक पहचान है। पत्र लेखन विधा में एक विशिष्ट शैली का उपयोग किया जाता है। पत्र सर्वप्रथम संबोधन से शुरू होता है। उसके बाद पत्र में जो कुछ बात पत्र लेखक को कहनी होती है, वे सभी क्रम से एक के बाद एक लिखी जाती हैं। लेकिन इसमें हमेशा इस बात पर जरूर जोर देना चाहिए कि पत्र की हर बात के तार आपस में जुडे रहें ताकि पाठक को समझने में आसानी हो। इसके अलावा यह भाषा शैली भी इसका एक विचारणीय बिंदु है। यदि आप पत्र अपने किसी मित्र या परिजन को लिख रहे हैं तो भाषा में अधिक औपचारिकता अनिवार्य नहीं, लेकिन फिर भी पत्र के आरंभ में व अंत में मूलभूत औपचारिकता निभाई ही जाती है। यदि बात की जाए प्रशासनिक पत्राचार की तो यहां लेखक की भाषा का पूरी तरह से औपचारिक होना अनिवार्य है। लेकिन इस बात को भी नहीं भूलना चाहिए कि पत्र की भाषा सरल हो ताकि पाठक तक आपका संदेश सरलता से पहुंच जाए। औपचारिकता निभाने के फेर में भाषा शैली को कठिन बना देना मूर्खता ही होगी। साथ ही भाषा का मधुर होना भी अति अनिवार्य है ताकि पाठक जब पत्र पढे तो उसे बेहतर महसूस हो। याद रहे कि पत्र के जरिए पाठक केवल आपके पदों से ही आपके भावों को समझने की कोशिश करता है। पत्र लेखन की इस कला को सीखने के लिए निरंतर अभ्यास आवश्यक है। शुरुआत में भाषा और शैली में कठिनाई हो सकती है, परंतु समय के साथ यह सहज होती जाती है। विद्यालयों में विद्यार्थियों को विभिन्न प्रकार के पत्र लिखने का अभ्यास कराया जाना चाहिए ताकि वे भविष्य में इस कला का उचित उपयोग कर सकें और अपने विचार प्रभावी ढंग से व्यक्त कर सकें।
title: Test #01: Pahla Patra - CPCT - 16/03/2024 - S2

text: तमिल भाषा और साहित्य के महान संत-कवि तिरुवल्लुवर द्वारा रचित तिरुक्कुरल केवल दक्षिण भारत या भारत तक सीमित ग्रंथ नहीं है। यह मानव जीवन के नैतिक और व्यावहारिक पक्षों पर विचार करने वाला एक कालजयी ग्रंथ है। इसकी रचना का काल निश्चित रूप से तय नहीं है, लेकिन इसे लगभग 2,000 वर्ष पुरानी तमिल साहित्यिक परंपरा का महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ माना जाता है। तिरु का अर्थ पवित्र या सम्मानसूचक है, जबकि कुरल संक्षिप्त छंद की ओर संकेत करता है। 1,330 कुरलों में तिरुवल्लुवर ने जीवन के गहरे सत्यों, नैतिक मूल्यों और सामाजिक व्यवहार को बेहद संक्षिप्त और प्रभावी ढंग से प्रस्तुत किया है। तिरुक्कुरल की सबसे बड़ी विशेषताओं में इसका व्यापक और सर्वसमावेशी चरित्र है। यह किसी एक संकीर्ण धार्मिक या सामाजिक दायरे तक सीमित नहीं है। इसमें नैतिकता, सामाजिक जीवन, शासन, अर्थव्यवस्था, मानवीय संबंधों और प्रेम जैसे विषयों पर विचार किया गया है। इसी व्यापकता के कारण इसे दुनिया की अनेक भाषाओं में अनूदित किया गया है। तमिलनाडु सरकार और विभिन्न संस्थानों के प्रयासों से इसके अनेक भारतीय और विदेशी भाषाओं में अनुवाद हुए हैं। तिरुक्कुरल का पूरा ढांचा तीन प्रमुख भागों अरम, पोरुल और इन्बम में विभाजित है। पहला भाग अरम सदाचार और नैतिक जीवन से संबंधित है। इसके 38 अध्यायों में सत्य, अहिंसा, दया, कृतज्ञता, आत्मसंयम और करुणा जैसे विषयों पर विचार किया गया है। तिरुवल्लुवर के विचार में सच्चा धर्म केवल बाहरी अनुष्ठानों में नहीं, बल्कि व्यक्ति के आचरण और मन की पवित्रता में दिखाई देता है। छल-कपट से दूर रहना और सभी जीवों के प्रति दया रखना ही वास्तविक नैतिकता का आधार है। दूसरा भाग पोरुल है, जिसमें 70 अध्यायों के माध्यम से राज्य व्यवस्था, प्रशासन, नेतृत्व, कूटनीति, अर्थव्यवस्था और सामाजिक जीवन पर विचार किया गया है। यह हिस्सा आधुनिक शासन और राजनीति के संदर्भ में भी विशेष रूप से महत्वपूर्ण दिखाई देता है। इसमें आदर्श शासक के गुणों, मंत्रियों की योग्यता, न्याय, सुरक्षा, मित्रता और राज्य संचालन जैसे विषयों पर व्यावहारिक दृष्टि मिलती है। तिरुवल्लुवर के अनुसार एक अच्छे राज्य में जनता को भूख, बीमारी और असुरक्षा से बचाने की जिम्मेदारी शासक की होती है। तीसरा भाग इन्बम या कामत्तुपाल है, जिसमें 25 अध्याय हैं। इसमें प्रेम, मानवीय भावनाओं, गृहस्थ जीवन और दांपत्य संबंधों का काव्यात्मक चित्रण मिलता है। यह बताता है कि भारतीय चिंतन परंपरा में मानव जीवन के सांसारिक पक्ष और भावनात्मक संबंधों को भी गंभीरता से देखा गया है। अंतरराष्ट्रीय संबंधों और आधुनिक राजनीति के दृष्टिकोण से तिरुक्कुरल का 'पोरुल' खंड विशेष महत्व रखता है। आज जब दुनिया युद्ध, आर्थिक असमानता, राजनीतिक अस्थिरता और अविश्वास जैसी चुनौतियों से जूझ रही है, तब तिरुवल्लुवर का सुशासन, न्याय और जिम्मेदार नेतृत्व पर जोर और भी प्रासंगिक लगता है। दुनिया के नेताओं के सामने इस ग्रंथ को रखना भारत की उस सांस्कृतिक कूटनीति का हिस्सा माना जा सकता है, जिसमें भारत केवल व्यापार और रणनीतिक साझेदारी की बात नहीं करता, अपितु अपनी विचार-संपदा को भी दुनिया के साथ साझा करता है। तिरुक्कुरल भारत की विचार-संपदा और अमूर्त ज्ञान-परंपरा का प्रतीक है तो तमिलनाडु के रामेश्वरम में स्थित रामनाथस्वामी मंदिर भारत की दृश्य वास्तुकला, स्थापत्य कला और धार्मिक-सांस्कृतिक परंपरा की निरंतरता का जीवंत उदाहरण है। यह मंदिर रामेश्वरम द्वीप पर स्थित है और हिंदू आस्था के प्रमुख तीर्थस्थलों में गिना जाता है। यह 12 ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिरों में से एक है। ब्रिक्स जैसे वैश्विक मंच पर तिरुक्कुरल जैसी कालजयी कृति को रूसी भाषा में प्रस्तुत करना और भारतीय स्थापत्य एवं सांस्कृतिक प्रतीकों को प्रमुखता देना इसी व्यापक दृष्टि की ओर संकेत करता है। यह संदेश देता है कि भारत दुनिया से संवाद करते समय केवल आर्थिक और रणनीतिक हितों की भाषा नहीं बोलता। वह अपनी सभ्यता की उस विचार-संपदा को भी सामने रखता है, जिसमें मानवता, नैतिकता, सुशासन और सांस्कृतिक विविधता के लिए महत्वपूर्ण संदेश निहित हैं।
title: Test #02: Tirukkural Kaljayi Granth Ewam Visheshta

text: 25 दिसम्बर, 1926 ईसवी को अतरसुइया, इलाहाबाद मे पिता चिरंजीवलाल वर्मा के घर मे जन्म लेनेवाला एक शिशु किस तरह से वय-वार्द्धक्य के साथ देश का एक महान साहित्यकार और पत्रकार के रूप मे रेखांकित होता रहा, वह विश्लेषण का विषय बन जाता है। धर्मवीर भारती ही थे, जिन्होंने अपने अव्यक्त प्रेम की शक्त वर्ज्य रेखा खींचकर अपने को एक ऐसे देवता की कोटि के अन्तर्गत ला खड़ा किया, जो गुनाह करता रहा, फिर भी देवता बना रहा। ऐसे सारस्वत हस्ताक्षर की शिक्षा-दीक्षा इलाहाबाद मे हुई थी, जिनमे अध्ययन के प्रति इतनी रुचि थी कि वे अपने मुहल्ले के ही हरिभवन पुस्तकालय में नियमित रूप से पुस्तकें पढ़ते रहे, जिसका मुख्य कारण था, आर्थिक अभाव से ग्रस्त उनका परिवार। वहीं के डीएवी हाईस्कूल से उन्होंने अपनी आरम्भिक शिक्षा अर्जित की थी। वे आठवीं कक्षा मे थे, तभी सिर पर से पिता का साया उठ चला था। इलाहाबाद मे रहनेवाले उनके मामा अभयकृष्ण जौहरी ने उन्हें अपना संरक्षण देते हुए, कायस्थ पाठशाला इंटर कॉलेज से इण्टरमीडिएट की शिक्षा करायी थी। डॉ. भारती का मन-प्राण क्रान्तिकारिता से ओत-प्रोत था; क्योंकि उस समय के पराधीन देश का वातावरण था ही ऐसा। उन्होंने भारत छोड़ो आन्दोलन में भाग लिया था, जिसके कारण उनका एक वर्ष प्रभावित हुआ था। उन्होंने स्नातक और स्नातकोत्तर की परीक्षाएं इलाहाबाद विश्वविद्यालय से उत्तीर्ण की थीं। उन्हें स्नातक की परीक्षा मे सर्वाधिक अंक अर्जित करने के कारण चिन्तामणि घोष मेडल प्रदान किया गया था। वे वही डॉ. धीरेन्द्र वर्मा थे, जिन्होंने मात्र पांच विद्यार्थियों को लेकर इलाहाबाद विश्वविद्यालय में हिन्दी-विभाग का प्रारम्भ कराया था। संयोग ऐसा रहा कि डॉ. भारती उसी विश्वविद्यालय मे हिन्दी का अध्यापन भी करने लगे थे। वहीं उन्होंने हिन्दीसाहित्य-कोश के कार्य में अपना महत्त्वपूर्ण योगदान किया था। उन्होंने निकष और आलोचना पत्रिकाओं का सम्पादन भी किया था। वे सारे साहित्यकार इलाहाबाद ही नहीं, देश की सारस्वत विभूति के रूप मे आज भी प्रतिष्ठित हैं। डॉ. भारती के भीतर साहित्य और पत्रकारिता का मनोरम संगम था। यही कारण था कि वे इलाहाबाद से ही प्रकाशित अभ्युदय समाचारपत्र में उसके सम्पादक पद्मकान्त मालवीय के सान्निध्य मे अंशकालीन कार्य करने लगे थे। उसके बाद इलाचन्द जोशी के सम्पादन मे प्रकाशित संगम पत्रिका के सहकारी सम्पादक बनाये गये थे। उन्होंने हिन्दुस्तानी एकेडमी में उपसचिव के पद पर भी कार्य किया था। वे व्यक्तिगत रूप से घर-घर जाकर शिक्षणकर्म भी करते रहे, जिससे कि उनका आर्थिक पक्ष चीखकर उन्हें अपने होने का एहसास न कराये। डॉ. भारती को यहीं से साहित्यिक संस्कार मिला, जिसने गुनाहों का देवता और सूरज का सातवां घोड़ा का सर्जन कराया। इलाहाबाद के कर्नलगंज, इलाहाबाद विश्वविद्यालय, सिविल लाइन्स इत्यादिक मुहल्ले गुनाहों का देवता के साक्षी बनते रहे, जिसकी आधारभूमि अतरसुइया ही रही। जब वे अपने प्रेम को संभालने और अव्यक्त को व्यक्त रूप देने में विफल रहे तब उनका प्रणय-पंछी एक ऐसी दिशा मे उड़ने के लिए पंख पसार चुका था, जिसका लौट पाना लगभग सम्भव नहीं था तब डॉ. धर्मवीर भारती इलाहाबाद को हमेशा के लिए त्यागकर बम्बई चले जाने का परिपक्व विचार बना चुके थे। उन्होंने 4 सितम्बर, 1997 ईं को बम्बई में मृत्यु की गोद मे जाने से पहले चन्दर और सुधा की अमर प्रेम-कहानी में इलाहाबाद की सड़कों, गलियों, मौसम और बौद्धिक वातावरण मे जिस भावप्रवणता का ताना-बाना बुना है और जो मर्मस्पर्शी-हृदयहारी वितान ताना है, वह उनका जिया और भोगा हुआ यथार्थ है, जिसे वे अन्तत:, गुनाहों का देवता के माध्यम से व्यक्त कर देते है:–रही बात उनके प्रतिष्ठित उपन्यास सूरज का सातवां घोड़ा की, तो वह भी इलाहाबाद के मुहल्ले अतरसुइया और जिन अन्य मुहल्ले के परिवार वातावरण के साथ डॉ. भारती का सरोकार था, वहां के निम्न और मध्यमवर्गीय परिवार के आर्थिक-सामाजिक संकट और संत्रास को, उन्होंने जिस रूप में साक्षी दिया था, उसका प्रभाव है।
title: Test #02: Dharmvir Bharti, Allahabad Aur Gunahon Ka Devta

text: थायरॉइड की बीमारी हो गई तो जिंदगी भर वजन, कमजोरी, बांझपन और दवाओं से संघर्ष ही नियति है। विज्ञान अधिकांश ऐसी धारणाओं का समर्थन नहीं करता। सबसे प्रचलित भ्रम वजन को लेकर है। हाइपोथायरॉइडिज्म से वजन बढ़ सकता है, लेकिन अधिकांश लोगों में यह वृद्धि बहुत अधिक नहीं होती। थायरॉक्सिन हाइपोथायरॉइडिज्म की दवा है, वजन घटाने की नहीं। आमतौर पर कुछ किलो वजन बढ़ता है और उसका कुछ हिस्सा शरीर में नमक और पानी रुकने से होता है। इसलिए यदि वजन 15 या 20 किलो बढ़ गया है, तो पूरा कारण थायरॉइड को मानना ठीक नहीं। उचित थायरॉक्सिन खुराक के बाद टीएसएच और टी4 सामान्य हों, लेकिन मोटापा बना रहे, तो भोजन, शारीरिक गतिविधि, नींद, तनाव, दवाओं, आनुवंशिक प्रवृति और इंसुलिन रेजिस्टेंस जैसे कारणों को देखना चाहिए। थायरॉइड है, इसलिए बांझपन होगा जैसी धारणा गलत है और अनावश्यक तनाव पैदा करती है। एक और भ्रम आधुनिक वेलनेस संस्कृति ने पैदा किया है-सेंधा, गुलाबी या हिमालयन नमक को आयोडीनयुक्त नमक से बेहतर मानना। असली प्रश्न है कि नमक पर्याप्त आयोडीन देता है या नहीं। आयोडीन थायरॉइड हार्मोन के निर्माण के लिए अनिवार्य है और गर्भावस्था तथा बचपन में इसकी कमी मस्तिष्क विकास को प्रभावित कर सकती है। आयोडीनयुक्त नमक सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य की बड़ी सफलता है। इसलिए गैर-आयोडीनयुक्त नमक अपनाना समझदारी नहीं। ज्यादा आयोडीन भी ठीक नहीं, लक्ष्य पर्याप्तता है, अति नहीं। थायरॉइड जांच को लेकर भी एक उपयोगी बात समझनी चाहिए। टीएसएच में दिनभर प्राकृतिक उतार-चढ़ाव होता है। इसलिए फॉलोअप जांच लगभग समान समय पर व संभव हो तो सुबह कराना बेहतर है। थायरॉक्सिन लेने वालों में कई बार सुबह की गोली से पहले रक्त का नमूना देना रिपोर्टों की तुलना को अधिक स्पष्ट बना सकता है। बच्चों में थायरॉइड को हल्के में लेना गंभीर गलती हो सकती है। थायरॉइड हार्मोन मस्तिष्क और शारीरिक वृद्धि के लिए जरूरी है। यदि किसी बच्चे की लंबाई अपेक्षित गति से नहीं बढ़ रही, वजन असामान्य रूप से बढ़ रहा है, वह सुस्त है, लगातार कब्ज रहता है या युवावस्था देर से शुरू हो रही है, तो उचित मूल्यांकन जरूरी है। लंबाई और वजन हर वर्ष ग्रोथ चार्ट पर दर्ज करना चाहिए। वृद्धि बचपन का महत्वपूर्ण जैविक संकेत है। सबसे संवेदनशील मामला नवजात शिशुओं का है। जन्मजात हाइपोथायरॉइडिज्म मिलने पर मां अक्सर स्वयं को दोष देने लगती है। अधिकांश मामलों में यह धारणा गलत है। अच्छी चिकित्सा केवल बीमारी का इलाज नहीं करती, वह डर, अपराधबोध और भ्रम भी दूर करती है। थायरॉक्सिन की ज्यादा खुराक वजन कम करा सकती है। जरूरत से अधिक थायरॉक्सिन लेने से चर्बी सुरक्षित तरीके से कम नहीं होती। इसके बजाय तेज धड़कन, हाथ कांपना, कमजोरी, हृदय संबंधी समस्याएं और हड्डियों तथा मांसपेशियों का नुकसान हो सकता है। खानपान को लेकर भी अनावश्यक डर है। गोभी, फूलगोभी, ब्रोकली, सरसों और सोया को अक्सर थायरॉइड खराब करने वाला भोजन बताया जाता है। सोया थायरॉइड ग्रंथि को नष्ट नहीं करता, लेकिन थायरॉक्सिन की गोली के तुरंत बाद या पहले लेने पर उसके अवशोषण को प्रभावित कर सकता है। समाधान सोया बंद करना नहीं, बल्कि दवा और भोजन के बीच पर्याप्त समय रखना है। कुछ लोग बेहतर महसूस करते ही खुद से थायरॉक्सिन की खुराक कम कर देते हैं या दवा छोड़ देते हैं, जबकि हाइपोथायरॉइडिज्म में यह निर्णय डॉक्टर की सलाह और जांच रिपोर्ट के आधार पर ही लेना चाहिए। गर्भावस्था के दौरान थायरॉइड हार्मोन की आवश्यकता बढ़ जाती है, इसलिए गर्भवती महिलाओं में टीएसएच की नियमित निगरानी विशेष महत्व रखती है। खुराक में देरी से समायोजन शिशु के मस्तिष्क विकास को प्रभावित कर सकता है। बुजुर्गों में थायरॉइड के लक्षण अक्सर उम्र बढ़ने के सामान्य बदलाव समझ लिए जाते हैं, जिससे निदान में देरी होती है। इसलिए थकान, वजन में बदलाव या मनोदशा में अंतर दिखने पर उचित जांच कराना समझदारी है।
title: Test #03: Thyroid Hormone Ke Baare Mein Jaanein

text: प्रत्येक युग में दुर्वासनिक, अहंकारिक, दमनकारी मायावी और पाशविक शक्तियों के बल पर दैत्य और राक्षसगण राज्य सत्ता के लिए बड़ी चुनौती के रूप में सामने आकर जहां अधर्म, अनाचार और आतंक का साम्राज्य स्थापित करने हेतु धर्म संस्कृति को नैस्तनाबूद करते हुए सामाजिक ताने-बाने को छिन्न-भिन्न करने का प्रयास करते है, वहीं धर्मारुढ़, ईश्वर प्रणिधान और भक्ति संपन्न दैवी शक्तियों को त्रास देते हुए उन्हें ईश्वर से विमुख करने का भी षड्यंत्र करते हैं। दैविक और राक्षसी शक्तियों का यह संघर्ष प्रत्येक युग में आकार लेता हुआ दिखाई देता है, किंतु जब यह संघर्ष असीमित आकार ग्रहण कर लेता है, तब निर्गुण, निराकार ब्रह्म सगुण, साकार रूप में कभी कृष्ण कभी राम और कभी नरसिंहादि रूपों में अवतरित होकर अत्याचारी और दुष्ट मायावी शक्तियों का संहार करते हैं। श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता में भगवान् श्री कृष्ण द्वारा अर्जुन को दिए गए ज्ञान की सरल व्याख्या अनुसार जब भी धर्म का ह्रास और अधर्म की वृद्धि होने लगती है, तब भक्तजनों का उद्धार एवं दुष्टों का विनाश कर धर्म की स्थापना करने को भगवान् युग-युग में प्रकट होते हैं। भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण का इस धरा धाम पर अवतरण केवल आसुरी शक्तियों के विनाश और धर्म स्थापना के लिए ही नहीं होता है, अपितु वे अपने प्रेमी भक्तों को अपनी दिव्य लीलाओं के माध्यम से आत्मानंद प्रदान करने के निमित्त भी अवतार ग्रहण करते हैं। यदि केवल दैत्यों, दानवों या राक्षसों का विनाश कर धर्म स्थापना ही निमित्त होता, तो मात्र उसके लिए निर्गुण भगवान् को सगुण रूप धारण करने की आखिर क्या जरूरत हो सकती थी? श्री भगवान् यदि केवल संकल्प भर कर लेते तो भी क्षणांश में ही संपूर्ण जगत् की समस्त आसुरी शक्तियां स्वयंमेव समाप्त हो जाती, और तत्क्षण धर्म राज्य की स्थापना हो जाती। निश्चियात्मक रूप से कहा जा सकता है कि भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण का इस धरा धाम पर अवतरण केवल आसुरी शक्तियों के विनाश और धर्म स्थापना के लिए ही नहीं हुआ था, अपितु वे अपने प्रेमी भक्तों को अपनी दिव्य लीलाओं के माध्यम से आत्मानंद प्रदान करने के निमित्त भी अवतरित हुए, भगवान् श्री कृष्ण ने सगुण, साकार रूप धरकर जहां धर्म राज्य की स्थापना की, वहीं अपने प्रेमी भक्तों को दिव्यातिदिव्य प्रेमामृत प्रदान किया। श्री रामचरितमान में तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि देवी पार्वती के श्री रामावतार के बारे में प्रश्न करने पर भगवान् शिव कहते हैं- देवी! श्रीरामचन्द्रजी के जन्म लेने के अनेक कारण हैं, जो एक से एक बढ़कर विचित्र हैं। भगवान् शिव कहते है-जब धर्म का ह्रास होता है, नीच अभिमानी राक्षसों की वृद्धि होकर अन्याय बढ़ जाता है, ब्राह्मण, गौ, देवता और पृथ्वी कष्ट पाते हैं, तब वे कृपा निधान भांति भांति के दिव्य शरीर धारण कर सज्जनों की पीड़ा हरते हैं। वे असुरों का अंत करते हैं, वैदों की मर्यादा की रक्षा करते हैं, और जगत् में अपना निर्मल यश फैलाते हैं, उसी यश को गा गाकर प्रभु के भक्तजन भवसागर से तर जाते हैं। कृपा के सागर वे भगवान् अपने प्रेमी भक्त जनों के हितार्थ शरीर धारण करते हैं। श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता की टीका साधक संजीवनी में महात्मा रामसुखदासजी महाराज लिखते हैं कि सर्वसमर्थ भगवान् अवतार लिए बिना भी संतजनों की रक्षा, दुष्टों का विनाश और धर्म की स्थापना कर सकते हैं, किंतु वे अपने प्रेमी भक्तों को प्रभु के सान्निध्य प्राप्त करने की उनकी अंतर्निहित भावनाओं को पूर्ण करने के निमित्त से अवतार लेते हैं। धर्म राज्य की स्थापना करते हैं और जगत् में भय का वातावरण समाप्त कर सबको निर्भयता प्रदान करते हैं और केवल यही नहीं बल्कि आनंद कंद भगवान अपने निज जनों को अपना दिव्य प्रेमानंद प्रदान कर उनकी जन्म जन्मांतरों की अभिलाषाओं को भी पूर्ण कर देते हैं। इस तरह श्रीभगवान् जीवों पर विशेष कृपा करने हेतु स्वयं को मनुष्य रूप में प्रकट कर ऐसी लीलाएं करते हैं।
title: Test #03: Dharm Ki Sthapana Karne - Shri Krishna

text: रामनाथस्वामी मंदिर द्रविड़ स्थापत्य कला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। इसका निर्माण और विस्तार कई शताब्दियों में विभिन्न शासकों और राजवंशों के संरक्षण में हुआ। मंदिर की सबसे बड़ी वास्तुशिल्पीय विशेषताओं में इसके विशाल गलियारे शामिल हैं। लगभग 1,200 मीटर लंबा यह गलियारा 1,212 अलंकृत स्तंभों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। इन स्तंभों पर की गई बारीक नक्काशी तत्कालीन शिल्पकारों की दक्षता और स्थापत्य कौशल को दर्शाती है। मंदिर परिसर में 22 पवित्र कुएं भी हैं, जिनका धार्मिक महत्व विशेष है। रामनाथस्वामी मंदिर की वास्तुकला और उसकी सांस्कृतिक महत्ता को अंतरराष्ट्रीय आयोजनों में भारत की विरासत के प्रतीक के रूप में प्रस्तुत करना इसलिए महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह देश की आधुनिक पहचान को उसकी प्राचीन जड़ों से जोड़ता है। भारत आज तकनीक, अर्थव्यवस्था, विज्ञान और रणनीतिक क्षमता के क्षेत्र में आगे बढ़ रहा है, लेकिन उसकी पहचान केवल आधुनिक उपलब्धियों से नहीं बनती। उसके पीछे हजारों वर्षों की सभ्यता, दर्शन, साहित्य, कला और स्थापत्य की एक लंबी परंपरा भी है। इसे चार धामों में से एक रामेश्वरम से भी जोड़ा जाता है। भारतीय धार्मिक परंपरा में काशी और रामेश्वरम के बीच एक विशेष आध्यात्मिक संबंध माना जाता है। काशी से गंगाजल लाकर रामेश्वरम में अभिषेक करने की परंपरा भी इसी सांस्कृतिक संबंध को दर्शाती है। यह परंपरा इस बात का प्रतीक है कि भौगोलिक रूप से विशाल और विविधताओं से भरा भारत लंबे समय से तीर्थ परंपराओं और सांस्कृतिक संबंधों के माध्यम से एक-दूसरे से जुड़ा रहा है। पौराणिक कथाओं के अनुसार रावण का वध करने के बाद भगवान राम ने समुद्र तट पर भगवान शिव की पूजा के लिए शिवलिंग स्थापित करने का संकल्प लिया। मान्यता है कि हनुमान जी कैलाश से शिवलिंग लाने गए थे, लेकिन उनके लौटने में विलंब हुआ। तब माता सीता ने रेत से शिवलिंग बनाया, जिसकी पूजा भगवान राम ने की। इसे रामलिंगम कहा जाता है। बाद में हनुमान द्वारा लाए गए शिवलिंग की भी स्थापना की गई। यह कथा भारतीय परंपरा में शैव और वैष्णव आस्थाओं के सुंदर समन्वय का प्रतीक मानी जाती है। यही भारत की सांस्कृतिक कूटनीति की वास्तविक शक्ति है। आधुनिक भारत जब वैश्विक मंच पर खड़ा होता है तो उसके साथ केवल उसकी आर्थिक ताकत नहीं होती, बल्कि रामेश्वरम की स्थापत्य परंपरा और सदियों पुरानी भारतीय सभ्यता की स्मृति भी साथ होती है। यही विरासत भारत को विश्व के सामने केवल एक उभरती हुई शक्ति के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि एक गहरी और जीवंत सभ्यतागत परंपरा वाले राष्ट्र के रूप में प्रस्तुत करती है। यह केवल औपचारिक उपहार या सजावटी व्यवस्था भर नहीं है। इसके पीछे विश्व मंच पर भारत की प्राचीन ज्ञान परंपरा, नैतिक दर्शन और सांस्कृतिक विरासत को सामने रखने का भाव दिखाई देता है। यह घटनाक्रम बताता है कि भारत की सांस्कृतिक सामर्थ्य की जड़ें उसकी उस प्राचीन विरासत में हैं, जिसने सदियों से मानव जीवन में न्याय, करुणा, सुशासन और आत्मानुशासन जैसे मूल्यों को महत्व दिया है। ब्रिक्स 2026 शिखर सम्मेलन के अवसर पर विश्व के प्रमुख नेताओं के समक्ष रामनाथस्वामी मंदिर की झलक प्रस्तुत करना भारत की सांस्कृतिक कूटनीति का एक सशक्त प्रयास माना जा सकता है। इस तरह के आयोजन केवल राजनयिक शिष्टाचार तक सीमित नहीं रहते, बल्कि वे मेजबान देश की सभ्यतागत गहराई को भी उजागर करते हैं। रामेश्वरम जैसे तीर्थ स्थल का उल्लेख यह संदेश देता है कि भारत विविधता में एकता के सिद्धांत पर सदियों से चलता आया है। वसुधैव कुटुंबकम् अर्थात पूरी पृथ्वी को एक परिवार मानने की भारतीय अवधारणा ऐसे वैश्विक मंचों पर स्वाभाविक रूप से प्रासंगिक हो जाती है। मंदिर की स्थापत्य कला, उसकी पौराणिक पृष्ठभूमि और उससे जुड़ी आस्था की परंपराएं मिलकर अंतरराष्ट्रीय अतिथियों के मन में भारत के प्रति गहरा सम्मान उत्पन्न करती हैं।
title: Test #04: Ramnathswami Mandir - Dravid Sthapatya Kala

text: प्रधानमंत्री ने आर्थिक विकास दर में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि पर देशवासियों को बधाई देते हुए एक बार फिर गैर जरूरी सोने की खरीद न करने, विदेश यात्रा से परहेज करने और साथ ही विदेश में शादी करने से बचने की अपील की। इसके साथ ही उन्होंने स्वदेशी का मंत्र भी दोहराया और देश को आत्मनिर्भर बनाने की आवश्यकता भी रेखांकित की। इस बार उन्होंने यह अपील इंस्टाग्राम पर वीडियो जारी करके की। इसके पहले उन्होंने ऐसी ही अपील कुछ माह पहले तब की थी, जब पश्चिम एशिया संकट के चलते तेल के दाम बढ़ रहे थे। तब उन्होंने वर्क फ्राम होम को प्राथमिकता देने और पेट्रोलियम पदार्थों की खपत कम करने का भी आग्रह किया था। देखना है कि उनकी ओर से नए सिरे से की गई अपील आम जनता पर कितना असर दिखाती है या नहीं? चूंकि भारत अपनी आवश्यकता का अधिकांश सोना आयात करता है और इसके चलते चालू खाता घाटा बढ़ता है, इसलिए उसकी खरीद से बचने में ही समझदारी है। ऐसा इसलिए भी किया जाना चाहिए, क्योंकि सोने से कोई नियमित आय नहीं होती। सोने के प्रति तमाम आकर्षण के बाद भी लोगों को यह समझना होगा कि यह निवेश का उचित विकल्प नहीं है, लेकिन इसी के साथ सरकार को भी इस पर चिंतन-मनन करना होगा कि आखिर वोकल फार लोकल यानी स्वदेशी वस्तुओं की खरीद का अभियान गति क्यों नहीं पकड़ पा रहा है? आज भारत में क्रय क्षमता से लैस एक ऐसा बड़ा मध्यवर्ग है, जो गुणवत्ता वाली वस्तुएं खरीदना पसंद करता है। वह ऐसी वस्तुएं विदेश से इसलिए खरीदता है, क्योंकि भारत में वे या तो आसानी से उपलब्ध नहीं हैं या फिर विदेश के मुकाबले महंगी पड़ती हैं। आज यह अपेक्षा नहीं की जानी चाहिए कि लोग स्वदेशी के नाम पर देश में निर्मित कम गुणवत्ता वाली वस्तुएं खरीदना पसंद करेंगे। आखिर भारतीय कारोबारी वैसी गुणवत्तायुक्त वस्तुएं क्यों नहीं बना पा रहे हैं, जिनकी भारतीय मध्य वर्ग के बीच मांग है?
